definition_zh: 金融稳定；金融体系稳健；（监管语境）不出现系统性危机的状态
definition_en: the condition in which the financial system performs its functions without serious disruption or crisis
core_image: 一排立在地基上的柱子，每根都稳稳受力，没有一根开始倾斜
scene: 每年春天，央行都会发布一份报告，评估银行体系能否承受冲击。 Every spring the central bank publishes a report on financial stability, asking whether banks can absorb shocks.
sceneCN: 每年春天，央行都会发布一份报告，评估银行体系能否承受冲击；句中的 financial stability 指「金融体系整体不出现系统性危机的状态」（第 1 个义项：金融体系整体稳定）。图中可辨识物件：报告封面、柱状图表、银行大楼、天平。

pos.zh: 金融稳定；金融体系稳健状态
金融稳定的；维护金融稳定的

senses.title: The system as a whole staying sound
senses.titleCN: 金融体系整体保持稳健
senses.definition: the state in which the whole financial system keeps working through shocks without a systemic crisis
senses.definitionCN: 整个金融体系在冲击下仍能运转、不爆发系统性危机的状态
senses.example: Every spring the central bank publishes a report on financial stability, asking whether banks can absorb shocks.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天，央行都会发布一份报告，评估银行体系能否承受冲击。
senses.why: Finance names the settling of debts and stability names standing firm, so the phrase pictures a debt system that does not topple.
senses.whyCN: finance 指债务的结清，stability 指站得稳，因此这个短语描绘的是一个不会倒下的债务体系。

senses.title: Banks and institutions being well capitalized
senses.titleCN: 金融机构资本充足、运转稳健
senses.definition: the soundness of individual banks and financial institutions, measured by capital, liquidity and asset quality
senses.definitionCN: 单个银行与金融机构的稳健程度，以资本、流动性与资产质量衡量
senses.example: Stress tests found the major banks sound enough to support financial stability.
senses.exampleCN: 压力测试发现各大银行足够稳健，可以支撑金融稳定。
senses.why: A system stands only if its members stand, so the phrase is also used of the institutions that make it up.
senses.whyCN: 体系只有成员站得住才站得住，因此这个短语也用于构成体系的机构。

senses.title: Prices and markets not swinging wildly
senses.titleCN: 市场价格与交易秩序平稳
senses.definition: the absence of extreme price swings, bubbles or market disruptions that damage confidence
senses.definitionCN: 不出现破坏信心的剧烈价格波动、泡沫或市场中断
senses.example: Regulators watched the housing market for signs that financial stability was at risk.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者密切注视房地产市场，寻找金融稳定受威胁的迹象。
senses.why: A market is stable when it can absorb shocks without violent swings, the same image of standing firm applied to prices.
senses.whyCN: 市场能吸收冲击而不剧烈摆动，就是稳定；同一「站得住」的画面被用到价格上。

senses.title: Households not overburdened with debt
senses.titleCN: 家庭财务稳健、债务可控
senses.definition: the condition of households whose debts and repayments remain manageable during downturns
senses.definitionCN: 家庭债务与还款在衰退期仍处于可控范围的状态
senses.example: High household debt is now treated as a risk to financial stability.
senses.exampleCN: 高企的家庭债务如今被视为对金融稳定的风险。
senses.why: When private balance sheets crack, the system cracks with them, so the phrase extends to the household level.
senses.whyCN: 私人资产负债表一旦裂开，体系也随之裂开，因此这个短语延伸到家庭层面。

senses.title: Firms able to service their debts
senses.titleCN: 企业财务稳健、偿债无碍
senses.definition: the condition of companies whose earnings cover their obligations even when conditions tighten
senses.definitionCN: 企业在环境收紧时收益仍能覆盖债务的状态
senses.example: Cheap credit had masked weak corporate financial stability.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价信贷掩盖了企业财务稳健性的薄弱。
senses.why: The corporate sector is another layer of the same standing structure, and its balance sheets carry the phrase's meaning.
senses.whyCN: 企业部门是同一稳固结构的又一层，其资产负债表承载着这个短语的含义。

senses.title: A mandate given to regulators
senses.titleCN: 监管当局承担的职责目标
senses.definition: the policy objective assigned to central banks and regulators, who must act before risks become crises
senses.definitionCN: 授予央行与监管机构的政策目标，须在风险演变为危机前行动
senses.example: The new law made financial stability an explicit mandate of the central bank.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律把金融稳定明确规定为央行的职责。
senses.why: A condition worth protecting becomes a duty once an institution is told to keep it, so the phrase turns into a mandate.
senses.whyCN: 一种值得守护的状态，在被指定给某个机构维持之后就变成职责，因此这个短语转为授权。

senses.title: Stability across borders
senses.titleCN: 国际与跨境的金融稳定
senses.definition: the shared condition of several national systems linked by trade, lending and capital flows
senses.definitionCN: 由贸易、借贷与资本流动联结的多个国家体系共同的稳定状态
senses.example: A currency run in one region can threaten financial stability elsewhere.
senses.exampleCN: 一个地区的挤兑可能威胁其他地区的金融稳定。
senses.why: Capital crosses borders faster than rules do, so the phrase is also used for the international layer of the same structure.
senses.whyCN: 资本跨境的速度快于规则，因此这个短语也用于同一结构的国际层面。

senses.title: A formal assessment of that condition
senses.titleCN: 金融稳定评估（报告与指标）
senses.definition: the periodic official assessment, with indicators and scenarios, of how far the system is from crisis
senses.definitionCN: 以指标与情景定期对体系距危机有多远所作的官方评估
senses.example: The autumn financial stability assessment flagged rising leverage.
senses.exampleCN: 秋季的金融稳定评估警示了杠杆上升。
senses.why: What is watched must be measured, so the name of the condition also labels the report that grades it.
senses.whyCN: 被守护的东西必须被测量，因此这种状态的名称也用来称呼为它打分的报告。

intro.en: Financial stability joins finance, from Old French finance 'settlement of a debt' and Latin finis 'end', with stability, from Latin stabilis 'firm' and stare 'to stand'. The pair became a policy term in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: financial stability 由 finance 与 stability 合成：finance 经古法语指「债务的结清」，源自拉丁 finis「终点」；stability 出自拉丁 stabilis「稳固」，再溯至 stare「站立」。这一搭配在二十世纪成为政策术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Finis meant 'end, boundary, limit'; settling a debt was pictured as bringing it to an end.
items.cn: finis 意为「终点、边界、限度」；结清债务被设想成把这件事带到终点。

items.en: Old French finance named the action of settling or paying, and English borrowed it for money matters and later for the management of money.
items.cn: 古法语 finance 指结清或支付的动作，英语借来表示钱财事务，后来又指资金管理。

items.en: Stare 'to stand' produced stabilis 'firm, standing steady', the root of stable, stability and stabilize.
items.cn: stare「站立」产生 stabilis「稳固、站得稳」，是 stable、stability 与 stabilize 的词根。

items.en: Twentieth-century central banking turned the two words into one term for the condition supervision exists to protect.
items.cn: 二十世纪的央行监管把这两个词合成一个术语，指监管所要守护的那种状态。

items.en: After the crises of the 1990s and 2008 the phrase became standard in international reports, with indicators, stress tests and periodic assessments.
items.cn: 经历九十年代与二零零八年的危机之后，这个短语成为国际报告的标准用语，配有指标、压力测试与定期评估。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring phrases built like this one but pointing at different objects; group two holds nouns for the quality of standing firm.
note.cn: 第一组是结构相似但指向不同对象的邻近短语；第二组是表示「站得稳」这一性质的词。

entries.definition: Soundness of government budgets and debt; it looks almost identical but concerns the treasury, not banks and markets.
entries.definitionCN: 指政府预算与债务的稳健；形式几乎相同，但关注国库，不是银行与市场。

entries.definition: A stable price level and currency, usually the target of interest-rate policy rather than of supervision.
entries.definitionCN: 指物价与币值稳定，通常是利率政策而非监管的目标。

entries.definition: Having enough money to live without fear; it applies to people, while financial stability applies to systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指有足够的钱生活而无忧；用于人，金融稳定则用于体系。

entries.definition: The body of rules governing finance; stability is the condition those rules aim at.
entries.definitionCN: 指治理金融的规则体系；稳定是这些规则想要达到的状态。

entries.definition: The quality of being financially healthy and well founded, often said of a bank or a currency.
entries.definitionCN: 指财务健康、基础牢靠，常用于银行或货币。

entries.definition: The capacity to absorb a shock and recover; stability is the state, resilience is the strength behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指承受冲击并恢复的能力；稳定是状态，韧性是背后的力量。

entries.definition: The quality of continuing to work under heavy strain, often used of systems and models.
entries.definitionCN: 指在重压下仍能运作的性质，常用于系统与模型。

entries.definition: A balance in which opposing forces cancel out; it is a theoretical state, not a supervisory goal.
entries.definitionCN: 指相互对抗的力量彼此抵消的平衡；是理论状态，不是监管目标。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Finance as the settling of debts plus stability as standing firm: a debt system that does not topple.
normal.cn: 金融是债务的结清，稳定是站得稳：一个不倒下的债务体系。

normal.en: The family runs finance, financial, stable, stability, stabilize and destabilize.
normal.cn: 同族词有 finance、financial、stable、stability、stabilize 与 destabilize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: safeguard financial stability, threats to financial stability, the financial stability report.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出政策义：维护金融稳定、对金融稳定的威胁、金融稳定报告。

normal.en: Central banks pair it with supervision: stability is what supervision exists to protect.
normal.cn: 央行把它与监管配对：稳定正是监管所要守护的东西。

normal.en: The two halves come from different Latin words, one for an ending and one for standing.
normal.cn: 两半来自不同的拉丁词，一个指终点，一个指站立。

abstract.en: Picture a row of columns sharing one foundation, so none can settle without the others noticing.
abstract.cn: 想象一排柱子共享一个地基，任何一根下沉都会被其余察觉。

abstract.en: Picture a tightrope walker whose pole never tips past the point of no return.
abstract.cn: 想象一个走钢丝的人，长杆始终没有倾过不可挽回的那一点。

abstract.en: Picture a ship held level by many small corrections no passenger ever feels.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船靠许多乘客感觉不到的小修正保持水平。

examples.en: The committee meets quarterly to review financial stability risks.
examples.cn: 该委员会每季度开会审议金融稳定风险。

examples.en: Rapid credit growth can undermine financial stability.
examples.cn: 信贷快速增长可能损害金融稳定。

examples.en: Cross-border lending links the financial stability of both countries.
examples.cn: 跨境借贷把两国的金融稳定联结在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 一排柱子共享一个地基，没有一根开始倾斜 → 金融稳定

root: 英语复合短语：financial（出自拉丁 finis「终点」，经古法语指债务结清）+ stability（出自拉丁 stabilis「稳固」，再溯至 stare「站立」）；指金融体系不发生系统性危机的稳健状态。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one standing structure: the whole system, its institutions, market prices, household balance sheets, corporate balance sheets, the supervisory mandate, the cross-border layer, and the assessment that grades it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个「站稳的结构」：整个体系、其中的机构、市场价格、家庭资产负债表、企业资产负债表、监管职责、跨境层面，以及为它打分的评估。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: columns sharing one foundation, none of them beginning to tilt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排共享地基的柱子，没有一根开始倾斜。

branches.en: WHOLE STRUCTURE: the system is stable when it keeps standing through a shock.
branches.cn: 整体结构：体系在冲击下仍然站住，就是稳定。

branches.en: PARTS AND PRICES: banks and market prices are the visible members and signals of the same structure.
branches.cn: 成员与价格：银行与市场价格是同一结构可见的成员与信号。

branches.en: PRIVATE LAYERS: household and corporate balance sheets are lower floors that carry the structure.
branches.cn: 私人层面：家庭与企业资产负债表是承托这个结构的下面几层。

branches.en: DUTY: a condition worth keeping becomes a mandate once an authority is told to guard it.
branches.cn: 职责：值得守护的状态，在当局被指定守护之后成为职责。

branches.en: WIDER AND MEASURED: capital flows widen the structure, and assessment turns it into a score.
branches.cn: 更宽与可测：资本流动把这个结构拓宽，评估把它变成分数。

intro.en: Financial stability joins an ending word and a standing word, and both families build many English terms.
intro.cn: financial stability 由「终点」词与「站立」词合成，两个词族都构成不少英语术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis supplies finance, financial and final; Latin stare supplies stable, stability, stabilize and constant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 finis 给出 finance、financial 与 final；拉丁 stare 给出 stable、stability、stabilize 与 constant。

items.example: Settling a debt was seen as reaching an end.
items.exampleCN: 结清债务被看作走到一个终点。

items.example: The root pictures something that does not fall.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘不倒下的东西。

items.meaning: settlement of a payment; money management

items.exampleCN: 这家公司陷入财务困境。

items.example: Prices stayed stable through the year.
The stability of the currency reassured savers.
items.exampleCN: 货币的稳定让储户安心。

items.example: Rate cuts helped stabilize the market.
items.exampleCN: 降息帮助市场稳定下来。

definition_zh: adj. 可传染的；可传达的
definition_en: able to be passed from one person to another
core_image: 拥挤车厢里一个人咳嗽，周围的人下意识后退
scene: 这种病在密切接触者之间可以传染。 The disease is communicable between close contacts.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：communicable 指可传染的；句意是这种病在密切接触者之间可以传染。

pos.zh: 可传染的；可传达的

senses.title: Able to spread between people
senses.definition: able to pass from one person to another, as a disease
senses.definitionCN: 像疾病那样能从一个人传给另一个人
senses.example: Measles is highly communicable.
senses.exampleCN: 麻疹传染性很强。
senses.why: Latin communicare means to share.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 communicare 意为共享。

senses.title: Able to be passed on as knowledge
senses.definition: able to be communicated as an idea or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 可作为想法或情感被传达
senses.example: Good writing makes complex ideas communicable.
senses.exampleCN: 好的写作让复杂想法变得可传达。
senses.why: The sharing root covers both disease and ideas.
senses.whyCN: 「共享」词根同时覆盖疾病与思想。

intro.en: Communicable comes from a Latin verb meaning to share.
intro.cn: communicable 源自拉丁语「共享」的动词。

items.en: Communis means shared or common.
items.cn: communis 意为共同的。

items.en: Communicare means to share or impart.
items.cn: communicare 意为分享、传达。

items.en: The adjective means able to be shared.
items.cn: 该形容词意为可分享的。

items.en: English used it of ideas first.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语先用它说思想。

items.en: It now mainly describes disease.
items.cn: 现代医学中主要形容疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the commun- shape; the near-meaning group names how disease spreads.
note.cn: 形近组共享 commun- 词形；近义组列出疾病传播的说法。

entries.definition: Spread by contact.

entries.definition: Caused by germs that spread.
entries.definitionCN: 传染性的。

entries.definition: Able to be passed on.
entries.definitionCN: 可传播的。

normalIntro.cn: 能被共享的东西，都可以是 communicable。

normal.en: Communis means shared.

normal.en: Communicare means to share.
normal.cn: communicare 意为分享。

normal.en: A shared illness is communicable.

normal.en: A shared idea is communicable too.

normal.en: Doctors use it for disease.
normal.cn: 医生用它形容疾病。

abstract.cn: 拥挤车厢里的一声咳嗽。

abstract.en: A story passed mouth to mouth.

abstract.en: A seed carried by wind.

sensesIntro.en: One word for a shared germ and a shared idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个词既指共享的病菌，也指共享的想法。

definition_zh: 人科演化；人科（含大猿与人类）这一支的演化史
definition_en: the evolutionary history of the family Hominidae, the great apes and humans
core_image: 一张树状图上，人类那一支被画在猿类中间，不在树顶
scene: 展厅的树状图上，人类那一支被画在猿类中间，而不是树顶。 Hominid evolution looks less like a march to the top than like a family album with missing pages.
sceneCN: 这里「人科演化」指人科这一支的演化史（第 1 个义项：科级演化史）；句意为这里的人科演化与其说像向顶端进军，不如说像一本缺页的家庭相册。

collocations.phrase: the fossil record of hominid evolution

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 homo（人）+ -idae（科级词尾）→ 人科成员：演化叙述中的主体
拉丁 evolutio「展开」→ 演化（语义偏移：从书卷展开到形态逐代展开）

senses.example: Hominid evolution looks less like a march to the top than like a family album with missing pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的人科演化与其说像向顶端进军，不如说像一本缺页的家庭相册。
senses.why: Hominidae marks the family and evolutio marks the unrolling, so the phrase covers every branch of that family, not only the human one.
senses.whyCN: Hominidae 标记科，evolutio 标记展开，因此这个短语覆盖该科的每一支，而不只人类这一支。

senses.title: The traditional narrow sense
senses.titleCN: 旧日窄义：仅指人类这一支的演化
senses.definition: in older writing, the evolution of the human line only
senses.definitionCN: 旧文献中仅指人类这一支的演化
senses.example: Older textbooks titled hominid evolution and meant only the ancestors of people.
senses.exampleCN: 旧教科书题为「人科演化」，实际只指人类的祖先。
senses.why: Because hominid once excluded the other apes, the phrase inherited that restriction; the same title now covers much more than its first readers expected.
senses.whyCN: 由于 hominid 曾排除其他猿类，这个短语继承了那一限制；同样的标题如今覆盖的范围远超最初读者的预想。

senses.title: The fossil sequence
senses.titleCN: 化石序列：可被排列的那串证据
senses.definition: the ordered series of fossils from which the history is reconstructed
senses.definitionCN: 据以重建这段历史的化石序列
senses.example: The fossil record of hominid evolution is thickest where sediments are volcanic.
senses.exampleCN: 火山沉积所在之处，人科演化的化石记录最厚。
senses.why: A history is invisible; a sequence of dated specimens is readable. The phrase shifts to the evidence whenever a claim must be checked against what has been found.
senses.whyCN: 历史看不见，定过年的标本序列却可读。每当主张需要对照实物检验，这个短语就转向证据。

senses.title: Anatomical transitions
senses.titleCN: 解剖转变：骨盆、牙齿与颅骨的变化
senses.definition: the anatomical changes, such as bipedalism, tooth reduction and brain expansion
senses.definitionCN: 骨盆、牙齿与颅骨等方面的解剖变化，如两足行走、牙齿缩小与脑扩大
senses.example: Hominid evolution is read from a pelvis before it is read from a skull.
senses.exampleCN: 人科演化先从骨盆读出，然后才从颅骨读出。
senses.why: Bones are the only direct evidence of ancient bodies, so the phrase's core chapters are anatomical; each transition is a change in a named structure.
senses.whyCN: 骨骼是古代身体唯一的直接证据，因此这个短语的核心章节是解剖的；每一次转变都是某一具名结构的变化。

senses.title: Adaptive and behavioural change
senses.titleCN: 适应与行为变化：食性、社会与工具
senses.definition: shifts in diet, social organisation and tool use treated as adaptations
senses.definitionCN: 把食性、社会组织与工具使用视为适应的变化
senses.example: Hominid evolution includes a diet that moved from leaves to roots and meat.
senses.exampleCN: 人科演化包括食性从叶子转向根茎与肉。
senses.why: Evolution selects on behaviour as well as bone, and behaviour can be inferred from teeth, campsites and stone; this chapter therefore mixes anatomy with inference.
senses.whyCN: 演化既选择骨骼，也选择行为，而行为可从牙齿、营地与石器推断；因此这一章把解剖与推断混在一起。

senses.title: The effect of taxonomic revision
senses.titleCN: 分类修订的影响：名词改变如何改写故事
senses.definition: the way reclassification changes what the history is said to contain
senses.definitionCN: 重新分类如何改变这段历史的内容
senses.example: Hominid evolution expanded as a category the moment the great apes were admitted to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 大猿一被纳入这个科，人科演化作为一个范畴也随之扩大。
senses.why: Because the phrase is built on a rank name, any change in that rank rewrites the sentence; taxonomy is not background but part of the claim.
senses.whyCN: 由于短语建立在层级名上，层级一变，句子就要重写；分类不是背景，而是主张的一部分。

senses.title: Molecular evidence
senses.titleCN: 分子证据：基因与谱系分化时间
senses.definition: the genetic evidence that dates splits and tracks gene flow
senses.definitionCN: 为分化定年并追踪基因流的遗传学证据
senses.example: Molecular work pushed the split with chimpanzees back millions of years before the fossils did.
senses.exampleCN: 分子研究把与黑猩猩的分化时间推前了数百万年，早于化石所能显示。
senses.why: DNA carries a record that bones do not, so the phrase now covers divergence dates and interbreeding as well as skeletons.
senses.whyCN: DNA 携带骨骼所没有的记录，因此这个短语如今除骨架外也覆盖分化年代与杂交。

senses.title: The teaching narrative
senses.titleCN: 教学叙事：展厅与课本讲的那一版
senses.definition: the simplified account presented in museums, courses and documentaries
senses.definitionCN: 博物馆、课程与纪录片所呈现的简化叙述
senses.example: The hominid evolution on the wall ends with a figure holding a spear and then a phone.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上的人科演化以一个先持矛、后持电话的形象收尾。
senses.why: Any long history must be edited to be taught; the public version is a genuine sense, and its simplifications are what specialists attack.
senses.whyCN: 任何漫长的历史都必须经过剪辑才能教；公共版本是一个真实义项，而它的简化正是专家攻击的地方。

intro.en: The phrase joins a nineteenth-century family name to a Latin word for unrolling; the family name has been redefined, and that redefinition is part of the phrase's history.
intro.cn: 这个短语把 19 世纪的科名接在拉丁语「展开」一词上；科名曾被重新界定，而那次重新界定也是短语历史的一部分。

items.en: The family name was formed on the Latin stem homin- with the family ending -idae, and originally held humans and their extinct relatives.
items.cn: 科名以拉丁词干 homin- 加科级词尾 -idae 构成，最初只含人类及其已灭绝亲属。

items.en: Evolvere 'to roll out, unroll', from ex- plus volvere 'to roll', supplies the image of a folded record opened in order.
items.cn: evolvere「展开、卷开」由 ex- 加 volvere「卷」构成，提供把折叠记录按序打开的意象。

items.en: Evolutio named the act of unrolling and had no biological sense in classical Latin; the modern sense is an English development.
items.cn: evolutio 指展开动作，古典拉丁语中无生物学义；现代义是英语的发展。

items.en: Comparative genetics later placed the great apes inside Hominidae, so hominid evolution came to cover apes as well as people.
items.cn: 比较遗传学后来把大猿放进 Hominidae，于是人科演化也开始覆盖猿类。

items.en: DNA evidence redated major splits and revealed interbreeding, adding chapters that the fossil record alone could not supply.
items.cn: DNA 证据为各大分化重新定年，并揭示杂交，添进了仅靠化石无法提供的章节。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact phrase has no agreed first citation, and the deeper origin of homo behind homin- remains unknown, with the humus reading a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切短语没有公认的最早书证；homin- 背后的 homo 更深来源仍不明，与 humus 的读法是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the parallel phrases that differ only in their rank word; group two holds the disciplines and mechanisms that explain the history.
note.cn: 第一组是仅差层级词的平行短语；第二组是解释这段历史的学科与机制。

entries.definition: The history of the human line after the split; narrower than the family-level phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 分化之后人类这一支的历史；比科级短语窄。

entries.definition: The history of the tribe Hominini, which excludes the other great apes.
entries.definitionCN: 人族的历史，不含其他大猿。

entries.definition: A member of the family; the phrase names the history those members produced.
entries.definitionCN: 该科的一个成员；短语命名这些成员所造成的历史。

entries.definition: The capitalized family name, a category rather than a process.
entries.definitionCN: 首字母大写的科名，是范畴而非过程。

entries.definition: The field that reconstructs this history from fossils and archaeology.
entries.definitionCN: 靠化石与考古重建这段历史的学科。

entries.definition: The broad science of descent and selection, of which this history is one case.
entries.definitionCN: 研究谱系与选择的宽泛科学，这段历史只是其中一例。

entries.definition: The differential survival of variants; it explains but does not name the history.
entries.definitionCN: 变体的差异化存活；它作解释，但不命名这段历史。

entries.definition: The surviving remains taken as a body of evidence, not the interpretation built on them.
entries.definitionCN: 留存遗存作为证据总体，而非据其建立的解释。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real ranks, real chapters and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实层级、真实章节与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Hominidae is the family, evolutio is the unrolling: the phrase unrolls a whole family, not just our branch.
normal.cn: Hominidae 是科，evolutio 是展开：短语展开的是整个科，不只是我们这一支。

normal.en: The chapters are gait, teeth, brain, diet, tools, dispersal, genes, and the museum version.
normal.cn: 各章是步态、牙齿、脑、食性、工具、扩散、基因，以及展厅版本。

normal.en: The family runs Hominidae, hominid, hominin, human, evolution, evolutionary, paleoanthropology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 Hominidae、hominid、hominin、human、evolution、evolutionary、paleoanthropology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: the fossil record of hominid evolution, hominid evolution in Africa.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人科演化的化石记录、非洲的人科演化。

normal.en: Taxonomy is part of the claim: widen the family and the sentence widens with it.
normal.cn: 分类本身是主张的一部分：科一变宽，句子也跟着变宽。

abstract.en: Picture a family album whose missing pages are the ones everyone asks about.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家庭相册，缺的正是人人追问的那几页。

abstract.en: Picture a tree drawn on a wall, with our branch placed among the others rather than above them.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上画着一棵树，我们那一支被放在其他支之间，而不是其上。

abstract.en: Picture a label change that silently rewrites a museum's whole first room.
abstract.cn: 想象一次标签改动，悄悄改写了博物馆整个第一展厅。

examples.en: Hominid evolution is dated by volcanic layers more reliably than by tooth size.
examples.cn: 给人科演化定年，靠火山层比靠牙齿大小更可靠。

examples.en: The exhibition revised its hominid evolution chart after the new jaw was described.
examples.cn: 新下颌被描述之后，展览修改了它的人科演化图。

examples.en: Students often arrive believing hominid evolution is a single line upward.
examples.cn: 学生常带着「人科演化是一条向上的直线」这一想法来上课。

dict_mnemonic.text: hominid（人科的）+ evolution（展开）＝ 人科这一支的展开；记「人类那一支画在猿类中间，不在树顶」。

root: 新拉丁 Hominidae（拉丁 homo「人」+ -idae 科级词尾）+ 拉丁 evolutio「展开」，来自 evolvere（ex- + volvere「卷」）；homo 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unroll one family history: the whole family, the older narrow reading, the fossil sequence, the anatomical transitions, behaviour, the effect of reclassification, the molecular chapters and the museum version.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展开一段科级历史：整个科、旧日窄义、化石序列、解剖转变、行为、重新分类的影响、分子章节，以及展厅版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree diagram on a museum wall with the human branch drawn among the apes, not at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：博物馆墙上的树状图，人类那一支画在猿类之间，不在顶端。

branches.en: TWO SCOPES OF ONE TITLE: the whole family now, and the human line only in older texts.
branches.cn: 同一个标题的两种范围：如今的整个科，与旧文本里仅人类一支。

branches.en: READING THE BODY: a dated sequence of fossils, then pelvis, teeth and skull.
branches.cn: 读身体：先是定年的化石序列，再是骨盆、牙齿与颅骨。

branches.en: WHAT BONES ONLY SUGGEST: diet, society and tools inferred from teeth and campsites.
branches.cn: 骨头只能暗示的东西：由牙齿与营地推断食性、社会与工具。

branches.en: WHEN THE FRAME MOVES: reclassification widens the sentence, and DNA adds dates bones cannot give.
branches.cn: 框架移动时：重新分类拓宽句子，DNA 添进骨头给不出的年代。

branches.en: THE EDITED VERSION: the wall chart that ends with a figure holding a phone.
branches.cn: 剪辑版：以持电话的形象收尾的墙上图表。

intro.en: Both elements are borrowed, but the family name is a taxonomic formation and the second word is a Latin verb family, so each half can be read separately.
intro.cn: 两个成分都是借来的，但科名是分类学构造，第二个词是拉丁动词词族，因此两半可分别读出。

latinIntro.en: New Latin Hominidae supplies the first element; Latin evolvere and evolutio supply the second. The Greek-derived -idae is a taxonomic ending rather than a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁 Hominidae 提供前件；拉丁 evolvere 与 evolutio 提供后件。源自希腊的 -idae 是分类词尾，而非拉丁词根。

items.example: The stem appears in every rank name of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在该族的每个层级名中。

items.structure: New Latin family ending from Greek -idai
items.example: The ending marks the rank that the phrase's history covers.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记这段历史所覆盖的层级。

items.example: The noun names the actors in the history.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名历史中的行动者。

items.example: The prefix gives the direction of unrolling.
The root supplies the image behind the second word.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供第二个词背后的意象。

items.example: The noun carries the scroll image into biology.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把书卷意象带进生物学。

items.example: The adjective marks the framework of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记主张的框架。

items.example: The compound names the field that reads the record.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名读记录的那门学科。

items.example: The narrower word marks the human branch within the family.
items.exampleCN: 较窄的这个词标记科内的人类一支。

latinEntries.structure: Hominidae (New Latin, f. plural, family rank)
latinEntries.meaning: the family of humans and great apes

definition_zh: 尽心投入的；坚定的；忠诚的；（关系）承诺相守的；（罪行）已犯下的；（资金、资源）已投入的；已交托的；已交付委员会审议的
definition_en: giving wholehearted dedication to a person, cause or task; also the past participle of commit, used of crimes carried out, resources pledged and matters handed over
core_image: 深夜的工地，一个人把安全帽上的名字胶带按紧，蹲下去用手抹平最后一小段未干的混凝土
scene: 深夜的工地已经收工，塔吊的灯灭了，只有一个人还蹲在未干的混凝土旁，用抹子把边角一遍遍压平，安全帽上贴着写有自己名字的胶带。 She stayed committed to the project long after the visitors and the cameras had gone.
sceneCN: 这里 committed 形容「把心力真正投进去、不半途撤走的」（第 1 个义项：对事业或任务尽心投入）；句意为探访者与摄像机都离开之后，她仍留在工地收尾。可辨识物件：未干的混凝土、抹子、贴着名字胶带的安全帽、已经熄灭的塔吊灯。

pos.zh: 尽心投入的；坚定的；忠诚的；已犯下的
本词作动词时为其过去式与过去分词：交托；投入；犯下

forms.label: 动词现在分词（双写 t）

senses.title: Wholeheartedly dedicated
senses.definition: giving full effort and attention to a task or cause, and not withdrawing when it becomes hard
senses.definitionCN: 对任务或事业付出全部心力与注意，在变难时也不抽身
senses.example: She stayed committed to the project after the funding and the visitors had gone.
senses.exampleCN: 资金与访客都离开之后，她仍对这个项目尽心投入。
senses.why: The past participle of the verb for handing something over describes a person who has handed their effort over and left it there.
senses.whyCN: 那个表示「交出去」的动词的过去分词，形容一个人把心力交出去并留在那里。

senses.title: Firmly on one side
senses.definition: openly and steadily supporting a person, team or policy over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期公开而稳定地支持某人、某队或某项政策
senses.example: He is a committed supporter of the local league, rain or shine.
senses.exampleCN: 无论晴雨，他都是本地联赛坚定的支持者。
senses.why: Support that lasts turns the participle into an adjective of character, not of one act.
senses.whyCN: 持续的支持使这个分词变成形容品性的形容词，而不是形容一次行动。

senses.title: A relationship with a promise in it
senses.definition: describing a couple or partnership that has promised to stay together rather than keep other options open
senses.definitionCN: 形容一对伴侣或合作关系已许诺相守，而不是保留其他选择
senses.example: They described themselves as a committed couple after two years apart.
senses.exampleCN: 分居两年之后，他们说自己是一对承诺相守的伴侣。
senses.why: The word marks the moment when a private promise becomes a public shape of life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的正是私下承诺变成公开生活形态的那一刻。

senses.title: A crime already carried out
senses.definition: used of an offence that has actually been performed, in the passive constructions of the verb
senses.definitionCN: 在动词的被动结构里，指一桩实际已经实施的违法行为
senses.example: The offence was committed at midnight, when the cameras were switched off.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩罪行是在午夜、摄像机被关掉的时候犯下的。
senses.why: Latin committere also meant to begin or carry out an act, and that sense settled on crimes and offences.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 committere 也有「开始、实施」一义，这一义最终固定在罪行与违法行为上。

senses.title: Handed over to someone's care
senses.definition: used of something formally handed over, whether to a person, to writing, to memory or to an institution
senses.definitionCN: 指某物被正式交出去，或交给某人、写成文字、记入记忆，或交由某机构
senses.example: The records were committed to the archive before the office closed.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室关闭之前，这些记录已被交存档案馆。
senses.why: This is the literal sense of the Latin verb, still visible in the passive: a thing is committed, given into keeping.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁动词的字面义，在被动式里仍然看得见：东西被交出去，交人保存。

senses.title: Funds already pledged
senses.definition: used of money or resources formally set aside for a purpose and no longer available
senses.definitionCN: 指为某用途正式留出、已不能再挪用的资金或资源
senses.example: By March, most of the budget was already committed to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 到三月时，大部分预算已经投入到薪水里。
senses.why: Accounting speaks of committed funds because the money has been handed over in promise, even before it leaves the account.
senses.whyCN: 会计说「已承诺资金」，因为钱在离开账户之前，就已通过承诺交了出去。

senses.title: Sent to a committee for review
senses.definition: in parliamentary procedure, describing a bill or question that has been formally referred to a committee
senses.definitionCN: 在议会程序中，形容法案或动议已被正式交付某个委员会
senses.example: The bill was committed to a standing committee and did not return that session.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案被交付常设委员会，那一届会期没有再回到全院。
senses.why: A committee is literally a body to which a matter is committed, so the procedural phrase keeps the old image of transfer.
senses.whyCN: 委员会字面上就是「受托的群体」，因此这一程序说法保留了古老的转交意象。

senses.title: Already bound by one's own word
senses.titleCN: 已被自己先前的话绑住
senses.definition: describing someone who cannot easily change course because of a promise or step already taken
senses.definitionCN: 形容某人因先前的承诺或已迈出的一步，难以轻易改道
senses.example: We are already committed to the October deadline and cannot move it again.
senses.exampleCN: 我们已经对十月的截止日期作过承诺，不能再挪了。
senses.why: A commitment made in the past acts on the present, which is why the same participle can mean both devoted and trapped.
senses.whyCN: 过去作出的承诺会作用于现在，因此同一个分词既能指「尽心」，也能指「被绑住」。

intro.en: Committed is the past participle of commit, from Latin committere 'to entrust, hand over', built on com- 'together' and mittere 'to send, let go'. The -ed ending is the English past participle marker, and the form later became an adjective in its own right.
intro.cn: 本词是那个表示「交托、交付」的动词的过去分词，来自拉丁 committere「交托、交付」，由表示「共同」的拉丁前缀与 mittere「送出、放开」构成。词尾是英语过去分词的标记，这一形式后来独立成为形容词。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, let go, release', with the past participle missus. Source uncertain: its deeper origin is not settled, so any older form given for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放开、释放」，过去分词为 missus。一般认为，这个分词就是本词词干的来源。来源不确定：其更深来源未定，凡为其给出的更早形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Com- 'together' with mittere produced committere, 'to entrust, hand over, join', and also 'to begin or carry out an act'.
items.cn: 表示「共同」的拉丁前缀加 mittere 构成 committere，意为「交托、交付、使结合」，另有「开始或实施一桩行为」之义。

items.en: The past participle commissus named what had been entrusted or handed over, and from it came the noun commissio.
items.cn: 过去分词 commissus 指已被交托或交出的东西，名词 commissio 即由它而来。

items.en: Old French commetre kept both the sense of entrusting and the sense of perpetrating, and English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 commetre 同时保留「交托」与「实施」两义，英语在十四世纪借入了这个动词。

items.en: English formed the participle with -ed; the doubled t of committing and committed follows the rule that a stressed final consonant doubles before a vowel ending.
items.cn: 英语用规则词尾构成过去分词；本词的现在分词与过去分词都双写 t，遵循的是「重读闭音节末尾辅音在元音词尾前双写」的规则。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the origin of mittere is not established, and the earliest use of the participle as a pure adjective cannot be dated to a single year, so any pre-Latin form proposed is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：mittere 的来源尚未确立；这个分词最早在何时被当作纯形容词使用，也无法定到某一年，凡为其提出的拉丁语之前的形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds nouns from the same handing-over verb, plus one look-alike from a different root; group two holds adjectives of commitment that differ in what has been given and how firmly.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「交付」动词的名词，另有一个出自其他词根的形近词；第二组是表示投入的形容词，区别在于交出去的是什么、以及有多坚定。

entries.definition: The noun built on the same verb: it names the pledge itself, while the participle describes the person who has made it or the thing already handed over.
entries.definitionCN: 建立在同一动词上的名词：它指承诺本身，而分词则形容作出承诺的人或已经被交出去的事物。

entries.definition: Built on the same verb with a different ending: it names a task given to someone, the body that holds it, or a share paid for a sale.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词配不同词尾构成：它指交给某人的任务、承担该任务的机构，或为销售支付的提成。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of sending a person to prison or to a hospital, or for a burial; the participle describes the person after that act.
entries.definitionCN: 指把人送进监狱或送医的行为，也指下葬；分词则形容该行为之后的那个人。

entries.definition: It looks like a twin and even begins with com-, but it comes from Latin commendare, built on mandare 'to entrust with a charge', so it is not the same root as this word.
entries.definitionCN: 它看着像同族，甚至同样带有表示「共同」的拉丁前缀，但来自拉丁 commendare，其词根是 mandare「托付职责」，与本词并非同根。

entries.definition: Gives time and energy to a task, often as a settled habit; the word under study adds the weight of a promise behind that effort.
entries.definitionCN: 把时间与精力给了一桩任务，常已成为固定习惯；本词则在这份付出背后多了一层承诺的重量。

entries.definition: Driven by affection or reverence towards a person or cause; it is warmer and less formal than the word under study.
entries.definitionCN: 出于对某人或某项事业的感情或敬意而投入；它比本词更温暖，也更不正式。

entries.definition: Bound by a formal promise, often with money or honour staked; it stresses the promise rather than the daily effort.
entries.definitionCN: 受正式承诺约束，常押上金钱或名誉；它强调承诺，而不强调日常的付出。

entries.definition: Firmly and unshakeably loyal, especially in politics or conflict; it describes the supporter rather than the work done.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定而不动摇地忠诚，尤用于政治或冲突；它形容支持者，而不形容做成的工。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real send root, the real family of the base verb, the spelling rule that doubles the t, and the two faces of the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「送出」词根、基础动词真实的同族词、使 t 双写的拼写规则，以及这个动词的两张面孔。

normal.en: The base verb is com- 'together' plus mittere 'to send', so being committed means having sent one's effort somewhere and leaving it there.
normal.cn: 基础动词由「共同」加「送出」构成，因此尽心投入就是把自己的心力送到某处并留在那里。

normal.en: The family runs commit, commitment, committal, committee and uncommitted, all built on the same handing-over verb.
normal.cn: 同族词包括动词、名词、表示交付的名词、表示受托群体的名词，以及表示未承诺的形容词，都出自同一个「交付」动词。

normal.en: The double t is a spelling rule, not an accident: commit, commits, committing, committed.
normal.cn: 双写 t 只是拼写规则，不是偶然：原形、三单、现在分词、过去式与过去分词都守住这一规则。

normal.en: The verb has two faces, to commit a crime and to commit oneself to a cause, and the participle carries both.
normal.cn: 这个动词有两张面孔：犯下一桩罪，和投身于一项事业；分词同时承载两者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its uses: be committed to, deeply committed, committed funding, a committed relationship.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的用场：致力于某事、深度投入、已承诺的资金、承诺稳定的关系。

abstract.en: Picture a hand still smoothing concrete after every light has been switched off.
abstract.cn: 想象所有的灯都已关掉之后，还有一只手在把混凝土抹平。

abstract.en: Picture a signature already dry on a page that cannot be torn out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名已经干在一页撕不下来的纸上。

abstract.en: Picture a road that has been walked so often that turning back would cost more than going on.
abstract.cn: 想象一条已经走过太多遍的路，回头比继续走代价更大。

examples.en: The most committed volunteers were the ones nobody photographed.
examples.cn: 最尽心投入的那些志愿者，恰恰是没人拍照的人。

examples.en: The court found that the fraud had been committed over three years.
examples.cn: 法院认定这起欺诈是在三年间实施的。

examples.en: Half the budget was committed before the first contract was signed.
examples.cn: 第一份合同签署之前，一半预算就已经拨定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「共同 + 送出」加上已然——已经把自己交出去，就成了尽心投入

root: 拉丁 committere = 表示「共同」的拉丁前缀 + mittere「送出、放开」，原义「交托、托付、使结合」；过去分词词尾为英语标记；本词由那个表示「交托」的动词的过去分词转为形容词。mittere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one form: a participle that first describes effort handed over, then a person who stands on one side, a couple who promise to stay, a crime carried out, a thing given into keeping, money set aside, a bill sent to a committee, and finally someone bound by their own earlier word.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个形式展开：这个分词先形容交出去的心力，再形容站在一边的人、许诺相守的一对、已经实施的罪行、被交人保存的东西、被划出的钱、被送进委员会的法案，最后形容被自己先前的话绑住的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand still smoothing the last corner of concrete after every machine has stopped.
core.cn: 核心意象：所有机器都停下之后，还有一只手在把混凝土的最后一角抹平。

branches.en: EFFORT AND ALLEGIANCE: the same dedication shows as hours spent on a task or as steady support for a side.
branches.cn: 付出与归属：同一份投入，表现为耗在一桩任务上的工时，或表现为稳稳站在一边。

branches.en: PROMISE AND BINDING: a couple's promise and a deadline already accepted are the same word seen at the start and later on.
branches.cn: 承诺与束缚：伴侣之间的许诺与已经接受的截止日期，是同一个词在开头与后来两个时刻的样子。

branches.en: THE DEED: the verb's other face, where what is carried out is a crime.
branches.cn: 行为：这个动词的另一张面孔，被实施的对象是一桩罪行。

branches.en: HANDED TO A KEEPER: a record given to an archive and a bill sent to a committee are the same transfer.
branches.cn: 交给看管者：记录交存档案馆，与法案交付委员会，是同一个转交动作。

branches.en: MONEY ON A LEDGER: the sum is promised away before it is ever spent.
branches.cn: 账上的钱：这笔钱还没花出去，就已通过承诺许给了别人。

intro.en: This form is a verb base plus a participial ending; the prefix, root and ending can each be read, and the ending is what turned the verb form into an adjective.
intro.cn: 这个形式由动词词干加分词词尾构成；前缀、词根与词尾都能逐层读出，正是词尾把这个动词形式变成了形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin com- adds togetherness and mittere supplies sending; English then added its own participial ending, which is why this word looks Latin in front and English at the end.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「共同」的拉丁前缀添上共同之意，mittere 提供「送出」；英语随后加上自己的分词词尾，因此这个词前半像拉丁语，末尾却是英语。

items.structure: mittere, misi, missum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root supplies the act of sending something away from oneself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「把东西从自己这里送出去」的动作。

items.example: The prefix turns sending into joining.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「送出」变成了「结合」。

items.meaning: to entrust; to hand over; to carry out
items.example: The Latin verb supplies both the trusting and the criminal sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词同时提供「交托」与「犯罪」两义。

items.meaningCN: 已被交托的；已被交付的
items.example: The Latin participle already described something given into keeping.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁分词已经用来描述被交人保存的东西。

items.example: The ending marks the form as completed action rather than present activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把该形式标记为已完成的动作，而不是正在进行的动作。

items.structure: commit (English verb from Old French commetre)
items.meaning: to entrust; to pledge; to carry out
items.example: The council will commit the money before winter.
items.exampleCN: 议会将在入冬前把这笔钱拨定。

items.structure: commit + -ed (past participle used as an adjective)
items.meaning: dedicated; already handed over or carried out
items.meaningCN: 尽心投入的；已被交付或实施的
items.example: She stayed committed to the project long after the cameras had gone.
items.exampleCN: 摄像机离开很久之后，她仍对这个项目尽心投入。

items.structure: commit + -ment (from Latin -mentum, result of an action)
items.example: The bridge was rebuilt because one man's commitment outlasted two floods.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥得以重修，是因为一个人的承诺熬过了两场洪水。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 已被交托的；已被交付的

definition_zh: 主要地；占主导地位地；绝大多数地
definition_en: mainly, or in a way that holds the largest share or the strongest influence
core_image: 一片林子里九成是同一种树，其余只在林缘零星几棵
scene: 集市上几十个摊位卖的全是同一种粗布，只有两个摊子摆着别的东西。 The market is predominantly a cloth market, with only two stalls selling anything else.
sceneCN: 这里指集市在整体上以布市为主（第 1 个义项：大部分情况下、主要地）；句意为这个集市主要是布市，只有两个摊子卖别的东西。

pos.zh: 主要地；占主导地位地；绝大多数地

derivatives.zh: 支配的；显性的；显性性状

senses.title: For the most part
senses.definition: mainly, when describing what something is mostly like
senses.definitionCN: 描述某事物大体属何种情况时的「主要地」
senses.example: The region is predominantly agricultural.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区以农业为主。
senses.why: Prae- means in front or before, and dominari means to rule, so what is predominant rules the description from the front of the line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀表示「在前」，词根意为「统治」，因此占据主导者是从队列最前面统摄整体描述的那一项。

senses.title: Holding the majority in number
senses.definition: making up more than half of a countable group
senses.definitionCN: 在一个可数的群体中占一半以上
senses.example: The audience was predominantly female.
senses.exampleCN: 观众以女性为主。
senses.why: Counting is the plainest form of ruling: the larger part outnumbers the rest and therefore sets the tone of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 数数是「统治」最朴素的形式：较大的那部分在人数上压过其余，因而定下整体的调子。

senses.title: Dominating by influence
senses.definition: so that the strongest group or factor controls decisions
senses.definitionCN: 最强的一方或因素控制着决定
senses.example: Decision-making is predominantly in the hands of a few officials.
senses.exampleCN: 决策权主要掌握在少数官员手中。
senses.why: Here power, not number, is what rules; the adverb measures who actually decides rather than who is present.
senses.whyCN: 这里统摄局面的是权力而非人数；副词衡量的是谁真正决定，而不是谁在场。

senses.title: Forming the main ingredient
senses.definition: making up the largest part of a mixture or material
senses.definitionCN: 在混合物或材料中占最大份额
senses.example: The rock is predominantly quartz.
senses.exampleCN: 这块岩石的主要成分是石英。
senses.why: Mineralogy borrows the word for the mineral that holds the largest share of the mass, where ruling means occupying most of the substance.
senses.whyCN: 矿物学借这个词指占质量份额最大的矿物，这里的「统治」指占据物质的大半。

senses.title: Typically of one kind
senses.definition: in most cases of a stated kind, as a general pattern
senses.definitionCN: 在多数情况下属于所述类型，构成一般规律
senses.example: Winters here are predominantly dry.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的冬天多为干燥天气。
senses.why: A prevailing pattern is a ruler in time: it holds sway over most seasons without forbidding exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 气候上的主导型态是时间里的统治者：它在多数季节掌权，但不必排除例外。

senses.title: Prevailing in colour or style
senses.definition: appearing as the main colour or visual character
senses.definitionCN: 作为主要颜色或视觉特征出现
senses.example: The walls were predominantly white, with dark wooden beams.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面以白色为主，配深色木梁。
senses.why: The eye reads a large field as the ground of a picture, so the colour that fills it is literally predominant in the scene.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛把大片区域读作画面的底子，因此填满这片区域的颜色在视觉上确实「占据前景之外的全体」。

senses.title: In ancestry or composition
senses.titleCN: 以某种族群或来源为主
senses.definition: so that most members of a population come from one stated origin
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中多数成员来自所述来源
senses.example: The city's population is predominantly of rural origin.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的人口以农村出身者为主。
senses.why: Demography counts origins, and the largest origin group sets the profile of the population as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 人口学统计来源，最大的来源群体为整体人口定下轮廓。

senses.title: Above all, when ranking causes
senses.definition: as the main reason among several that could be named
senses.definitionCN: 在可以列出的多个原因中作为主要原因
senses.example: The failure was predominantly a matter of poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失败首要的是规划不当。
senses.why: Among competing explanations the dominant one carries the argument, so the adverb ranks causes rather than describing a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 在相互竞争的解释里，主导的那一个承担了论证，因此副词是在给原因排序，而不是描述人群。

intro.en: Predominantly is predominant plus -ly, and predominant is Latin prae-, in front, with dominari, to rule, from dominus, master. The medieval Latin form praedominari is recorded; the direct source is clear and only the English date is approximate.
intro.cn: predominantly 是 predominant 加 -ly；predominant 来自拉丁语 prae-「在前」加 dominari「统治」，后者出自 dominus「主人」。中古拉丁语有 praedominari 这一形式；直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Dominus is the master of a household, and it also gives English dominate and dominion.
items.cn: dominus 是一户之主，也给出英语 dominate 与 dominion。

items.en: The verb dominari means to be master, to rule, and it is the source of the ruling image in the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 dominari 意为做主、统治，是整个词族中「统治」意象的来源。

items.en: Prae- means before or in front; joined to dominari it yields the sense of ruling over others, standing first.
items.cn: prae- 意为在前、在旁；与 dominari 相连即得「凌驾于他人之上、站在最前」之义。

items.en: Scholastic and legal Latin use praedominari for holding the upper hand, and the participle passes into French and English.
items.cn: 经院与法律拉丁语用 praedominari 表示占上风，其分词形式传入法语与英语。

items.en: Predominant enters English in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, first in theology and then in general description.
items.cn: predominant 于十六、十七世纪进入英语，先用于神学，后用于一般描述。

items.en: The adverb predominantly is a later formation; its exact first date is uncertain, and it spreads with statistics and survey writing.
items.cn: 副词 predominantly 是较晚的构词，确切首见年代不确定，随统计与调查报告的写作而普及。

note.en: The first group shares the dominus ruling-root; the second group names majority without the image of a master.
note.cn: 第一组共享 dominus「主人」这一统治词根；第二组表示多数，但不带「主人」的意象。

entries.definition: Holding the largest share or the strongest position; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 占最大份额或最强地位的；副词所依托的形容词。

entries.definition: To be the strongest or most numerous element.
entries.definitionCN: 成为最强或数量最多的成分。

entries.definition: The state of holding the upper hand.
entries.definitionCN: 占上风的状态。

entries.definition: Ruling or most conspicuous, built on dominus without the prae- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 支配的、最显眼的，只用 dominus、不带 prae- 前缀。

entries.definition: To control or tower over others.
entries.definitionCN: 控制他人或高踞其上。

entries.definition: For the greater part; more than anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分；最主要地。

entries.definition: Above all other things, often ranking importance.
entries.definitionCN: 首要地，常用于排重要性。

entries.definition: To a great extent, with room left for exceptions.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上，留有例外余地。

entries.definition: In most cases or for most of the time.
entries.definitionCN: 在多数情况下或多数时间里。

entries.definition: First in rank or purpose, rather than in number.
entries.definitionCN: 在等级或目的上居首，而非数量上占多。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real dominus root, the real prae- prefix and the real survey phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 dominus 词根、真实的 prae- 前缀与真实的调查用语。

normal.en: Dominus is the master of the house, so predominant means the one that runs the place.
normal.cn: dominus 是一屋之主，所以 predominant 就是「管着这个地方」的那一个。

normal.en: Prae- puts the ruler in front, which is why the word also means standing first in a ranking.
normal.cn: prae- 把统治者放在最前，所以这个词也指在排序中居首。

normal.en: Survey reports love the phrase predominantly rural, because counting is the easiest way to be dominant.
normal.cn: 调查报告爱用「以乡村为主」这类说法，因为数数是最容易显出的主导。

normal.en: Predominantly white walls are not all white; the word always leaves room for the dark beams.
normal.cn: 「以白色为主」的墙面并非全白；这个词总给深色木梁留了位置。

normal.en: Predominant does not mean total: it means first among others, not alone.
normal.cn: predominant 不等于全部：它指在众者之中居首，而不是唯一。

abstract.en: What predominates sets the temperature of the room, even when it is not every person in it.
abstract.cn: 占主导者决定房间的温度，即便它不是屋里的每一个人。

abstract.en: Majority is a claim about weight, and weighting is how a crowd becomes a direction.
abstract.cn: 多数是关于分量的判断，而分量正是人群变成方向的方式。

abstract.en: The predominant colour is the one the eye stops noticing.
abstract.cn: 占主导的颜色，恰恰是眼睛不再注意的那一种。

examples.en: The workforce is predominantly young and predominantly urban.
examples.cn: 劳动力以年轻人为主，也以城市人口为主。

examples.en: Its exports are predominantly raw materials rather than finished goods.
examples.cn: 它的出口以原材料为主，而非成品。

examples.en: The debate was predominantly about cost, not about safety.
examples.cn: 这场争论主要围绕成本，而不是安全。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞多米南特利」，domi 让人想到「家庭」里做主的人：一家人里做主的那位，就是占主导地

root: 拉丁语 prae-「在前」+ dominari「统治」（出自 dominus「主人」）→ 中古拉丁语 praedominari「占上风」→ 英语 predominant，再加 -ly 成副词。直接来源清楚；英语首见年代为约数。同族 dominant、dominate、dominance 均出自 dominus，但都不带 prae- 前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all ask which side is bigger or stronger: the general character, the head count, the hand on the decision, the main ingredient, the usual weather, the colour that fills the field, the largest ancestry group, and the leading cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在问「哪一边更大或更强」：整体性质、人数、决策之手、主要成分、常见天气、填满画面的颜色、最大的来源群体，以及首要原因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forest where nine trees in ten are the same species.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片林子，十棵树里有九棵是同一树种。

branches.en: THE GENERAL CHARACTER: what something is mostly like, stated in one word.
branches.cn: 整体性质：用一句话说出某物大体是什么样子。

branches.en: THE COUNT: more than half of a group, measured by heads.
branches.cn: 计数：按人头算，超过群体的一半。

branches.en: THE HAND ON THE DECISION: influence rather than number holding the upper hand.
branches.cn: 决策之手：占上风的是影响力而非人数。

branches.en: THE BULK: the mineral that fills most of the rock, and the origin group that fills most of the population.
branches.cn: 主体：填满岩石大半的矿物，以及构成人口大半的来源群体。

branches.en: THE SETTING TONE: the usual weather, the colour that fills the wall, and the leading explanation.
branches.cn: 定调者：常见的天气、填满墙面的颜色，以及首要的解释。

intro.en: Predominantly is -ly on predominant, which is prae- plus dominari plus -ant. The Latin line is dominus, master, then dominari, to rule.
intro.cn: predominantly 是 -ly 加在 predominant 上，而 predominant 是 prae- 加 dominari 再加 -ant。拉丁语这条线是 dominus「主人」，再到 dominari「统治」。

latinIntro.en: Dominus and dominari carry the ruling sense; prae- adds position in front, and -ant and -ly only change the part of speech.
latinIntro.cn: dominus 与 dominari 承载「统治」义；prae- 加上「在前」的位置，-ant 与 -ly 只改变词性。

items.example: The noun supplies the figure of the one who rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「统治的那一位」这一形象。

items.example: The verb turns the master into the act of ruling.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「主人」变成统治的行为。

items.example: The prefix places the ruling element at the head of the line.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把统治的那一项放在队列最前。

items.example: It turns the verb into an adjective of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成表状态的形容词。

items.example: The shorter form marks the strongest element without the prefix.
items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的短形式标出最强的那一项。

items.example: The verb keeps the plain ruling sense of dominari.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留 dominari 平实的统治义。

items.example: The compound adds the idea of standing first among rivals.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式加上「在对手中居首」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the action behind the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是副词背后的动作。

items.example: The adverb lets the writer describe a whole in one word.
items.exampleCN: 副词让作者用一个词描述整体。

items.example: The noun names the state, not the manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指状态，而非方式。

definition_zh: 知识渊博的；在行的，内行的；显示出知识的
definition_en: having a lot of information or understanding about a subject, and able to use it well
core_image: 集市上一个摊主抬头就能指出哪家铺子的秤最准，问的人还没说完
scene: 集市上，游客问哪家铺子的秤最准，摊主一句话就指对了人。 The stallholder was knowledgeable about every supplier in the market.
sceneCN: 这里 knowledgeable 指「对某一范围了解很多且说得准」（第 1 个义项：见闻广博）；句意为这位摊主对市场里每个供货商都很在行。可辨识物件：摊位、秤、菜筐、手写的价牌。

pos.zh: 知识渊博的；在行的，内行的；显示出知识的

senses.title: Well informed in general
senses.definition: having a wide store of information and being able to draw on it
senses.definitionCN: 拥有广博的信息储备并能随时取用
senses.example: The stallholder was knowledgeable about every supplier in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这位摊主对市场里每个供货商都很在行。
senses.why: The suffix means 'having the quality', so the adjective says a person is full of what has been learned.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀意为「具有这种性质」，因此形容词表示一个人装满了所学之物。

senses.title: Expert in a field
senses.definition: possessing deep and reliable understanding of one subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题拥有深厚而可靠的理解
senses.example: She is knowledgeable about medieval tax records.
senses.exampleCN: 她精通中世纪税收档案。
senses.why: Depth, not breadth, is what separates an expert from someone merely well informed.
senses.whyCN: 是深度而非广度，把行家与仅仅见闻广的人区分开来。

senses.title: Showing knowledge
senses.definition: of an answer, question or remark, revealing that the speaker knows the subject
senses.definitionCN: 指回答、提问或言论显出说话者懂行
senses.example: He asked a knowledgeable question about the second clause.
senses.exampleCN: 他就第二条款提了一个很内行的问题。
senses.why: The adjective can describe the product of knowledge as well as the person who holds it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能描述知识的产物，也能描述持有知识的人。

senses.title: Well versed in a subject
senses.definition: familiar with the details and conventions of a field
senses.definitionCN: 熟悉某一领域的细节与惯例
senses.example: The technician was knowledgeable in electrical safety codes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位技术员熟悉电气安全规范。
senses.why: Familiarity with rules and details is a distinct kind of knowing, so the adjective takes 'in'.
senses.whyCN: 熟悉规则与细节是另一种知，因此这个形容词常接「在……方面」。

senses.title: Worth asking
senses.definition: of a person, reliable enough that others go to them for answers
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人可靠到别人会去找他求证
senses.example: For anything about the harbour, he is the knowledgeable one.
senses.exampleCN: 凡是关于港口的事，他才是懂行的那位。
senses.why: Knowledge becomes social when others route their questions through one person.
senses.whyCN: 当别人把问题都转给某一个人时，知识就变成了社会性的。

senses.title: A specialist audience
senses.definition: of a group, already carrying the background needed to follow a technical talk
senses.definitionCN: 指一群已具备听懂专业报告所需背景的人
senses.example: The lecture was aimed at a knowledgeable audience.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座面向有专业背景的听众。
senses.why: The adjective also measures the listener's store, not only the speaker's.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也衡量听者的储备，而不只是说话者的。

senses.title: Technically competent
senses.definition: having enough technical or legal knowledge to act correctly
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够的技术或法律知识以正确行事
senses.example: Only a knowledgeable operator should reset the valve.
senses.exampleCN: 只有懂行的操作员才该复位这个阀门。
senses.why: In technical settings, being knowledgeable is a safety requirement rather than a compliment.
senses.whyCN: 在技术场景里，懂行是安全要求，而不只是一句称赞。

senses.title: Carrying local knowledge
senses.definition: having the practical knowledge of a place that residents acquire
senses.definitionCN: 拥有居民才有的、关于某地的实用知识
senses.example: A knowledgeable neighbour warned us about the tide.
senses.exampleCN: 一位了解当地情况的邻居提醒我们注意潮水。
senses.why: Local knowledge is learned by living somewhere, which is why the adjective often describes guides and residents.
senses.whyCN: 当地情况靠住在那里学来，所以这个形容词常描述向导与居民。

intro.en: Knowledgeable is knowledge plus an English suffix meaning 'having the quality of'. The date is approximate.
intro.cn: knowledgeable 是表示「知识」的名词加一个表示「具有……性质」的英语后缀。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun for what is known supplies the whole stem, including its partly unexplained ending.
items.cn: 表示「所知之物」的名词提供整个词干，包括那个部分无法解释的词尾。

items.en: The suffix usually means 'able to be', but with nouns such as comfort or knowledge it means 'having the quality of'.
items.cn: 这个后缀通常表示「能够被」，但与表示安慰或知识的名词结合时，表示「具有……性质」。

items.en: The adjective is recorded from the early nineteenth century, when reviews needed a word for a well-stocked mind.
items.cn: 这个形容词自十九世纪初有记录，当时评论需要一个词来形容头脑充实的人。

items.en: It now appears mostly before nouns such as staff, audience, guide and operator, and after the preposition about.
items.cn: 它如今多出现在员工、听众、向导、操作员这类名词之前，以及「关于」这一介词之后。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest written use is not firmly dated, and the noun's own ending remains unexplained.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的书面用法年代不确，名词本身的词尾也仍无解释。

note.en: Group one holds words formed from the same knowing stem; group two holds the adjectives of competence it is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「知」词干的词；第二组是常与之混淆、表示能力的形容词。

entries.definition: Built on the same stem but with the passive sense, so it means 'able to be known', not 'full of knowledge'.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这一词干，但取被动义，意为「可被知道的」，而非「装满知识的」。

entries.definition: From the verb meaning 'to admit'; an acknowledged expert is recognised by others, which is a different claim.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「承认」的动词；「公认的」专家是被他人认可，这是另一种说法。

entries.definition: A compound describing an industry or system founded on information, not a person who holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，描述以信息为基础的行业或系统，而非持有信息的人。

entries.definition: Known by many people; fame says nothing about how much the person actually understands.
entries.definitionCN: 被许多人知道；名气并不说明此人实际懂多少。

entries.definition: Supplied with current facts, often about events; it stresses information rather than deep understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 掌握当前事实，常指时事；它强调信息而非深层理解。

entries.definition: Having special skill or knowledge in a field, usually certified by training or reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 在某领域有专门技能或知识，通常由训练或声誉证明。

entries.definition: Experienced and familiar with a subject's details, often used with 'in'.
entries.definitionCN: 有经验并熟悉某学科的细节，常与「在……方面」连用。

entries.definition: Having noticed something; awareness is far weaker than being knowledgeable.
entries.definitionCN: 已经注意到某事；知悉远比「在行」要弱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the noun stem, the suffix, and the prepositions that reveal the sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：名词词干、后缀，以及揭示词义的介词搭配。

normal.en: Knowledge plus a suffix meaning 'having the quality' equals a person full of it.
normal.cn: 表示「知识」的名词加上表示「具有这种性质」的后缀，等于一个装满知识的人。

normal.en: The preposition matters: knowledgeable about a subject, knowledgeable in a field.
normal.cn: 介词很要紧：对某主题在行，在某领域有专门知识。

normal.en: It usually describes people and their products: staff, guides, audiences and answers can all be knowledgeable.
normal.cn: 它通常描述人及其产物：员工、向导、听众与回答都可以是「内行的」。

normal.en: Compare knowable, which looks similar but means 'can be known', the opposite direction.
normal.cn: 对比表示「可被知道」的那个词：形似，却方向正相反。

normal.en: Being knowledgeable is a compliment; being expert is a credential; being informed is merely current.
normal.cn: 「在行」是称赞，「专家」是资历，「知情」只是掌握了近况。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer that opens without a search.
abstract.cn: 想象一个抽屉，不用翻找就能打开。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lights the whole room rather than one corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮整间屋子，而不只是一个角落。

abstract.en: Picture a map already folded into the right page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图早已翻到正确的那一页。

examples.en: The staff were knowledgeable and answered every question.
examples.cn: 员工很内行，回答了每个问题。

examples.en: A knowledgeable reader will notice the missing citation.
examples.cn: 内行的读者会注意到缺失的引注。

examples.en: He was knowledgeable about the river but not about the roads.
examples.cn: 他熟悉这条河，却不熟路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脑子里有货」——一开口就显出懂行 → 知识渊博的

root: knowledge（知识，古英语「知道」加名词词尾）+ 英语中表示「具有……性质」的后缀；英语 knowledgeable 指知识渊博、在行的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one well-stocked mind: full in general, deep in one field, visible in what the person says, familiar with details, worth consulting, present in an audience, reliable in technical matters and rooted in local experience.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一种充实的头脑：整体上见闻广、在某一领域有深度、从言谈中看得出来、熟悉细节、值得请教、也能出现在听众身上、在技术事务上可靠，并扎根于当地经验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawer that opens on the right answer without a search.
core.cn: 核心意象：一拉开就取出正确答案的抽屉。

branches.en: BREADTH: the adjective first says the store is large, without saying where it came from.
branches.cn: 广度：这个形容词首先说明储藏很大，却不说它从何而来。

branches.en: DEPTH: one field known down to its conventions, marked by the preposition 'in'.
branches.cn: 深度：某一领域连惯例都熟悉，由介词「在……方面」标出。

branches.en: WHAT OTHERS HEAR: a question or a lecture can show knowledge in the asker or the listener.
branches.cn: 别人听见的：一个提问或一场讲座，能在提问者或听者身上显出知识。

branches.en: THE PERSON OTHERS ROUTE QUESTIONS TO: knowledge becomes social when it is consulted.
branches.cn: 别人绕过去请教的人：知识在被请教时变成社会性的。

branches.en: RELIABILITY IN PLACE: technical safety and local tides both require knowing that a book cannot supply.
branches.cn: 在具体处境中的可靠：技术安全与当地潮汐都需要书本给不了的知。

intro.en: Knowledgeable is a two-piece English formation, and the same suffix behaves differently on nouns and on verbs.
intro.cn: knowledgeable 是两段式英语构词，同一后缀加在名词与动词上表现不同。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native English and the suffix reached English through Latin; the deep knowing root has Indo-European relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是英语本族，后缀经拉丁语进入英语；深层的「知」词根有印欧同族。

items.example: With nouns it describes a quality rather than a possibility.
items.exampleCN: 与名词结合时，它描述性质而非可能性。

items.example: The outcome is knowable in advance.
The rare negative form appears in reviews.
items.exampleCN: 这一罕用否定形式见于评论。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be; having the quality

definition_zh: 驯化；驯养；栽培；使适应家庭生活；使（条约）转为国内法
definition_en: to bring a wild animal or plant under human control and use
core_image: 一双手把一只挣扎的幼兽按在膝上，另一只手把门闩轻轻扣上
scene: 农人把野生的禾草一株株挑出来留种， Farmers domesticate the wild grass by saving seed from the calmest plants.
sceneCN: 这里 domesticate 指「把野生植物选育为栽培作物」（第 2 个义项：栽培化）；句意为农人从最安静的植株上留种，从而驯化这种野草。图中可辨识物件：留种穗、麻袋、挑选的手、田垄。

pos.zh: 驯化；驯养；栽培；使适应家庭生活
（罕用）已驯化的动物

senses.title: Tame an animal over generations
senses.definition: to breed and manage a wild animal population so that it lives under human care
senses.definitionCN: 繁育并管理野生兽群，使其生活在人类照料之下
senses.example: People domesticated dogs long before they kept herds.
senses.exampleCN: 人们养畜群之前很久就驯化了狗。
senses.why: the verb is the act behind domestication, and its object is a population rather than a single pet.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是驯化背后的动作，其对象是一个群体，而不是一只宠物。

senses.title: Turn a wild plant into a crop
senses.definition: to select and cultivate a wild plant until it depends on human sowing
senses.definitionCN: 对野生植物进行选育与栽培，直到它依赖人播种
senses.example: Early farmers domesticated barley without knowing genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 早期农民不懂遗传学，却驯化了二棱大麦。
senses.why: the plant sense repeats the animal sense at the level of seed rather than behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 植物义在种子层面重复了动物义，而不是在行为层面。

senses.title: Adapt a species genetically
senses.definition: to bring about inherited changes that suit a species to human environments
senses.definitionCN: 造成可遗传的改变，使某物种适应人类环境
senses.example: Selective breeding domesticated the temperament as well as the body.
senses.exampleCN: 选育既驯化了身体，也驯化了性情。
senses.why: when the change is heritable, taming one generation domesticates the line.
senses.whyCN: 当改变可遗传时，驯服一代就驯化了整条线。

senses.title: Accustom a person to home life
senses.definition: to make a person used to the routines and confines of a household
senses.definitionCN: 使人习惯于家户的日常与范围
senses.example: Years of indoor work had domesticated him more than he admitted.
senses.exampleCN: 多年室内工作使他安于家居，比他承认的更甚。
senses.why: the household image turns on a person, and the verb now means settling someone into domestic routine.
senses.whyCN: 家户意象转向人，动词于是指让人安于家庭日常。

senses.title: Make something familiar and manageable
senses.definition: to make an unfamiliar idea, tool or practice easy to live with
senses.definitionCN: 使陌生的想法、工具或做法易于共处
senses.example: The handbook domesticated a difficult theory for new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册把一套艰深理论变得新员工也能上手。
senses.why: anything wild or intimidating can be brought indoors metaphorically.
senses.whyCN: 任何野生或令人畏惧之物，都可以在比喻意义上被带进屋内。

senses.title: Incorporate a treaty into domestic law
senses.definition: in law, to give an international agreement effect within a national legal order
senses.definitionCN: 法律上使国际协定在国内法律秩序中生效
senses.example: Parliament domesticated the convention by statute.
senses.exampleCN: 议会以法规把该公约转为国内法。
senses.why: the international text must be brought into the house of national law before courts can apply it.
senses.whyCN: 国际文本必须先被带进国家法律这座房子，法院才能适用。

senses.title: A domesticated animal, as a rare noun
senses.titleCN: 作为罕用名词的驯化动物
senses.definition: rarely, a domesticated animal or plant considered as an entity
senses.definitionCN: 罕用，指作为实体的已驯化动植物
senses.example: The farm keeps four domesticates and a dozen wild species.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场养四种驯化种和十几种野生种。
senses.why: English often lets a verb form double as a noun, and specialists use it for the organism itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让动词形式兼作名词，专业人士用它指生物本身。

senses.title: Settle and work a landscape
senses.definition: to bring land into settled, managed use
senses.definitionCN: 把土地纳入定居、有管理的使用
senses.example: The valley was domesticated by terrace builders a thousand years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山谷在一千年前被修梯田的人驯化了。
senses.why: if a species can be brought into the household, so can the ground it grows on.
senses.whyCN: 既然物种能被带进家户，它生长的土地也可以。

intro.en: Domesticate comes from Latin domesticare 'to make domestic', built on domesticus 'of the household'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: domesticate 出自拉丁 domesticare「使家用、使驯服」，建于 domesticus「属于家户的」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Domus 'house' is the base of the family. Its deeper origin is reconstructed, and the common link to a building root remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: domus「房子」是整个词族的基础。其更深来源属重构，通常联系的「建造」词根仍是假说。

items.en: Domesticus described what belongs to a household, including animals kept indoors.
items.cn: domesticus 描述属于家户之物，包括养在屋内的动物。

items.en: Domesticare meant 'to make domestic, to tame'; it is the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: domesticare 意为「使家用、使驯服」，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: English domesticate is recorded in the seventeenth century, at first for animals and later for plants.
items.cn: 英语 domesticate 在 17 世纪有记录，先用于动物，后用于植物。

items.en: The verb was extended to people, tools and treaties; the legal use is recent and its first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词后来扩展到人、工具与条约；法律用法较晚，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin household family; the second lists other verbs of bringing something under control.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个拉丁「家户」词族；第二组是把某物置于控制之下的其他动词。

entries.definition: Of the home or of animals kept there; an adjective, where domesticate is the action.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭的或家养的；是形容词，domesticate 是动作。

entries.definition: Already tamed or adapted; it reports a result, while domesticate names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指已被驯化或适应；报告结果，而 domesticate 指做的动作。

entries.definition: The whole historical process; the verb can be one step inside that process.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个历史过程；动词可以是这个过程里的一步。

entries.definition: The state or quality of home life; it has no taming sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭生活的状态或性质；完全没有驯化含义。

entries.definition: To make one animal calm around people; it need not change the species or its offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 使单只动物在人前安静；不必改变物种或后代。

entries.definition: To prepare and tend land or plants; the labour can occur without any inherited change.
entries.definitionCN: 整地并照料土地或植物；这种劳动可以没有可遗传的改变。

entries.definition: To mate selected animals or plants; it is the mechanism often used to domesticate.
entries.definitionCN: 让选定的动植物交配；常是驯化所用的机制。

entries.definition: To establish a species in a new region; the aim is survival there, not human use.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物种在新地区立足；目标是当地存活，而非人类利用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin house verb, the regular English endings and the objects the verb takes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「房子」动词、规则的英语词尾，以及这个动词常带的宾语。

normal.en: domesticus 'of the house' + -are 'to make' = to make something house-broken.
normal.cn: domesticus「属于房子」+ -are「使」= 使某物适应屋内生活。

normal.en: The verb is regular: domesticates, domesticated, domesticated, domesticating.
normal.cn: 这个动词规则变化：domesticates、domesticated、domesticated、domesticating。

normal.en: Typical objects are animals, plants, species and treaties.
normal.cn: 典型宾语是动物、植物、物种与条约。

normal.en: The result adjective is domesticated, and the process noun is domestication.
normal.cn: 结果形容词是 domesticated，过程名词是 domestication。

normal.en: Domare 'to tame' looks related in meaning but is a separate Latin verb.
normal.cn: domare「使驯服」在意义上看似相关，却是另一个拉丁动词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing gently on a young animal until it stops struggling.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻按在幼兽身上，直到它不再挣扎。

abstract.en: Picture a door latch that can be opened from inside but not from outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一把门闩，从里面能开，从外面打不开。

abstract.en: Picture a wild field being taught to hold still in rows.
abstract.cn: 想象一片野地被教着站成一排排。

examples.en: Farmers domesticated rice in several river valleys independently.
examples.cn: 农民在几处河谷各自独立地驯化了水稻。

examples.en: You cannot domesticate a species in one lifetime.
examples.cn: 一个物种不可能在一代人的时间里被驯化。

examples.en: The state domesticated the agreement through a new act.
examples.cn: 该国以一部新法把该协定转为国内法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多麦斯提凯特」听成「多把麦子提进家」——野物提进家门，喂熟、留种，就是驯化。

root: 拉丁 domus「房子、家户」→ domesticus「属于家户的」→ domesticare「使家用、使驯服」，英语直接借其动词形作 domesticate。domare「使驯服」为另一动词，不与此同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from taming animals and plants through genetic adaptation, human domestication, familiarising ideas, legal incorporation, the rare noun and settled land.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从驯养动植物，经遗传适应、人的家居化、想法日常化、法律纳入、罕用名词，到土地的定居经营。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a young animal while the gate is latched.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按住幼兽，另一只手扣上门闩。

branches.en: BEAST AND CROP: behaviour and seed are two handles on the same act of bringing inside.
branches.cn: 兽与作物：行为与种子，是把同一「带进家户」动作的两个抓手。

branches.en: THE LINE AND THE THING: inherited change makes a lineage domestic, and the resulting organism can be counted.
branches.cn: 谱系与个体：可遗传的改变使一条谱系家养化，其结果生物也就可以计数。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a human can be settled into a household as surely as an animal.
branches.cn: 人：人也可以像动物一样被安顿进家户。

branches.en: THE IDEA: a difficult theory is brought indoors until ordinary people can live with it.
branches.cn: 想法：艰深理论被带进屋内，直到普通人能与它共处。

branches.en: LAW AND GROUND: a treaty enters national law, and a valley enters settled use.
branches.cn: 法律与土地：条约进入国家法，山谷进入定居使用。

intro.en: Domesticate is a Latin household adjective plus a Latin verb ending, with English tense endings added on top.
intro.cn: domesticate 是拉丁「家户」形容词加拉丁动词词尾，其上又加英语时态词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus gives domicile, domestic and domesticate; the taming verb domare is a different root and should not be folded in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 domus 给出 domicile、domestic、domesticate；表驯服的 domare 属另一词根，不应并入。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of indoors.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「屋内」的意思。

items.example: The ending makes a verb of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把形容词变成动词。
他们驯化了当地的谷物。

items.example: Domestication changed the diet of the region.
items.exampleCN: 驯化改变了该地区的饮食。

items.example: Domestic life settled around the hearth.
items.exampleCN: 家庭生活围绕炉灶展开。

items.example: The tax domicile is the family house.

derivatives.meaning: to tame a feral population again

definition_zh: 解放；使脱离控制、监禁或束缚；释放（气体等）；解放运动
definition_en: the act of setting someone free from control, confinement or a constraining condition
core_image: 牢门被推开，光从走廊尽头照进来，门槛上落着一串钥匙
scene: 清晨的营区大门被从里面推开，人们沿着泥路走出来，等在门外的家人举起写着名字的纸牌。 The archive records the liberation of the camp, the act of setting the prisoners free, in the spring of nineteen forty-five.
sceneCN: 这里 liberation 指「使被关押者脱离控制」（第 1 个义项：把人从拘禁中放出）；句意为档案记录了那处营地在四五年春天获得解放。可辨识物件：推开的大门、泥路、姓名纸牌、走廊尽头的晨光、落在地上的钥匙。

pos.zh: 解放；释放；解放运动（可数，复数 liberations）

senses.title: The act of setting someone free
senses.titleCN: 使某人获得自由的行为
senses.definition: the act of releasing a person or people from confinement, control or servitude
senses.definitionCN: 把人从拘禁、控制或奴役中放出的行为
senses.example: The archive records the liberation of the camp in the spring of nineteen forty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 档案记录了那处营地在四五年春天获得解放。
senses.why: liberare is 'to make free', from liber 'free'; the noun names the moment the condition changes.
senses.whyCN: liberare 是「使自由」，来自 liber「自由的」；名词指状态改变的那一刻。

senses.title: Military liberation of a place
senses.definition: the recapture or freeing of a territory by armed force
senses.definitionCN: 以武力收复或解救一片地区
senses.example: The liberation of the port cut the enemy's supply line.
senses.exampleCN: 港口的解放切断了敌方的补给线。
senses.why: armies describe recapture as liberation when they are welcomed as freeing the inhabitants.
senses.whyCN: 当军队被视为解救居民时，他们就把收复称为解放。

senses.title: National or colonial liberation
senses.definition: the ending of foreign rule and the achievement of independence
senses.definitionCN: 结束外国统治并取得独立
senses.example: National liberation movements reshaped the map after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后，民族解放运动重划了地图。
senses.why: a people under external rule experiences the end of that rule as a release, so the word joins national claims.
senses.whyCN: 受外来统治的民族把统治的结束体验为释放，因此这个词与民族诉求结合。

senses.title: Social liberation of a group
senses.definition: the removal of legal and social restraints from a class, gender or minority
senses.definitionCN: 解除对某一阶级、性别或少数群体的法律与社会束缚
senses.example: The liberation of women from restrictive property laws took decades.
senses.exampleCN: 女性从限制性财产法中的解放花了数十年。
senses.why: the word is borrowed from physical release to describe the removal of legal chains.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从身体释放借来，用来描述法律锁链的解除。

senses.title: Personal or intellectual liberation
senses.definition: a private release from fear, habit, ignorance or an oppressive belief
senses.definitionCN: 个人从恐惧、习惯、无知或压抑性信念中解脱
senses.example: Learning to read was a personal liberation for him.
senses.exampleCN: 学会阅读对他而言是一种个人的解放。
senses.why: the outer act has an inner analogue: what holds a mind can also be opened.
senses.whyCN: 外在动作有内在对应：锁住心智的东西也能被打开。

senses.title: A liberation movement or organization
senses.definition: an organized political force that describes its goal as liberation
senses.definitionCN: 以解放为目标的组织化政治力量
senses.example: The liberation front controlled three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 解放阵线控制着三个省。
senses.why: when a cause organizes, the abstract noun becomes part of its name.
senses.whyCN: 当一项事业组织起来，抽象名词就成为其名称的一部分。

senses.title: Release of a substance, especially a gas
senses.definition: the freeing of a gas, energy or chemical from a bound state
senses.definitionCN: 使气体、能量或化学物质从束缚状态中释放
senses.example: The liberation of gas from the rock warned the miners.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石中气体的释出警告了矿工。
senses.why: chemistry uses the same word for physical freeing, which shows how literal the core sense remains.
senses.whyCN: 化学用同一个词指物理释放，可见核心义仍然很字面。

senses.title: Abstraction: removal of any constraint
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何束缚的解除
senses.definition: any process by which a limit on action is removed, whether physical, legal or mental
senses.definitionCN: 任何解除行动限制的过程，无论物理、法律或心理
senses.example: Liberation begins when a rule loses its power to frighten.
senses.exampleCN: 当一条规则失去吓人的力量，解放就开始了。
senses.why: the deepest sense is negative: not the gaining of something new but the lifting of a weight.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是否定性的：不是获得新东西，而是移走一份重量。

intro.en: Liberation comes from Latin liberare 'to set free', from liber 'free'. The Latin word liber also means 'book' but is a different word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: liberation 来自拉丁 liberare「使自由」，源于 liber「自由的」。拉丁语中 liber 也指「书」，但那是另一个词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, unrestricted'; it is a different word from liber 'book', which belongs to another stem.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、不受限制的」；它与表示「书」的 liber 是另一个词，属不同词干。

items.en: Liberare meant 'to set free, release, acquit'; it turned the adjective into an action.
items.cn: liberare 意为「使自由、释放、宣告无罪」；它把形容词变成动作。

items.en: Liberatio named a setting free or acquittal, and English liberation came from this noun.
items.cn: liberatio 指释放或宣告无罪，英语 liberation 来自这个名词。

items.en: The word entered English through Old French in the fifteenth century, first in legal and religious senses.
items.cn: 这个词在十五世纪经古法语进入英语，最初用于法律与宗教语境。

items.en: From the eighteenth century liberation was applied to nations, slaves and social classes, and the political sense now dominates.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，liberation 被用于民族、奴隶与社会阶级，政治义如今占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin): the deeper root of liber is often reconstructed with a sense such as 'to grow up', but no single reconstruction is proven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语前来源）：liber 的更深词根常被重构为带有「成长」之义的形状，但没有哪一种重构得到证明。

note.en: Group one holds liberty-family words easily confused with liberation; group two holds neighbouring ideas of being freed.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 liberation 混淆的自由类词；第二组是「获得自由」的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The condition of being free; liberation is the act or process that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指自由的状态；liberation 是产生这一状态的行为或过程。

entries.definition: Originally 'befitting a free man', now a political and social label; it does not mean the act of freeing.
entries.definitionCN: 原指「适合自由人的」，现为政治与社会标签；不表示「解放」这个动作。

entries.definition: One who liberates; the noun names the agent, while liberation names the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施解放的人；名词命名施动者，而 liberation 命名行为。

entries.definition: Being saved from danger or captivity; it stresses rescue from a threat more than the ending of a system.
entries.definitionCN: 指从危险或囚禁中被救出；更强调脱离威胁，而非终结制度。

entries.definition: The formal legal freeing of a person from slavery or authority; liberation is broader and can be military or personal.
entries.definitionCN: 指法律上正式使某人脱离奴役或支配；liberation 更宽，可指军事或个人层面的解放。

entries.definition: The state of a nation governing itself; liberation can be the struggle that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家自治的状态；liberation 可以是产生它的斗争。

entries.definition: The act of letting a person or thing go; it is physical and neutral, without the political weight of liberation.
entries.definitionCN: 指放开人或物；是物理性、中性的，没有 liberation 的政治分量。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being constrained; liberation is one route to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受约束的一般状态；liberation 是通向它的一条路径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective, the real family and the physical picture of an opening door.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：那个拉丁形容词、真实词族，以及「门被打开」的身体图景。

normal.en: liber 'free' + -ation: the act of making free.
normal.cn: liber「自由的」+ -ation：使自由的行为。

normal.en: The family runs liberate, liberator, liberty, liberal, liberation, deliver.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 liberate、liberator、liberty、liberal、liberation、deliver。

normal.en: Do not confuse liber 'free' with liber 'book': same spelling, different stem.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 liber「自由的」与 liber「书」：拼写相同，词干不同。

normal.en: The core picture is a door opened from the inside.
normal.cn: 核心图景是一扇从里面被打开的门。

normal.en: Typical partners are national, movement, war of and women's.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「民族的」「运动」「……战争」与「妇女的」。

abstract.en: Picture a key left on the threshold after the lock has already been opened.
abstract.cn: 想象锁已打开之后，钥匙留在门槛上。

abstract.en: Picture a window opened in a room that had forgotten the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一间忘了天空的房间被打开一扇窗。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that still exists but no longer makes anyone afraid.
abstract.cn: 想象一条仍然存在却不再让人害怕的规则。

examples.en: The city celebrated its liberation with a quiet procession.
examples.cn: 这座城市以一场安静的游行庆祝解放。

examples.en: Literacy brought a kind of liberation that no law could grant.
examples.cn: 识字带来一种法律无法给予的解放。

examples.en: The experiment measured the liberation of hydrogen from the sample.
examples.cn: 实验测量了样品中氢气的释放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「lib（自由 libr）+ eration（变成）」——把人变成自由的状态 → 解放

root: 拉丁 liber「自由的」+ -atio（行为名词）→ liberatio「释放」。拉丁语 liber 另指「书」，属不同词干；liber 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one opening: a door is unlocked. The opening becomes a military recapture, a national end of foreign rule, a social removal of restraints, a private release, an organized cause, a chemical freeing and finally the lifting of any limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次开启展开：门被打开。这次开启先成为军事收复，再成为民族结束外来统治，再成为社会束缚的解除，再成为个人解脱，再成为组织化事业，再成为化学释放，最后成为任何限制的移走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lock opened from within, light entering a long corridor, keys left on the sill.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁从里面被打开，光进入长走廊，钥匙留在窗台上。
