branches.en: THE PHYSICAL OPENING: a person or a place is released by force or by arrival.
branches.cn: 身体开启：一个人或一个地方因武力或到来而获释。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE CLAIM: a people or a class claims release from a system.
branches.cn: 集体诉求：一个民族或阶级要求从制度中释放。

branches.en: THE INNER DOOR: what confined a mind can also be opened.
branches.cn: 内门：困住心智的东西也能被打开。

branches.en: THE ORGANIZED CAUSE: the noun becomes a banner for a movement.
branches.cn: 组织化事业：这个名词成为运动旗帜。

branches.en: THE LIFTED WEIGHT: chemistry and abstraction both mean a restraint removed.
branches.cn: 移走的重量：化学与抽象义都指束缚被解除。

intro.en: Liberation is a Latin adjective turned into an action noun, and the same stem builds a large English family.
intro.cn: liberation 是由拉丁形容词变成的行为名词，同一词干构成庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin liber and liberare give liberty, liberal, liberate, liberation and deliver; the separate liber 'book' gives library and libretto.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 liber 与 liberare 衍生 liberty、liberal、liberate、liberation 与 deliver；另一个 liber「书」衍生 library 与 libretto。

items.example: The adjective described a free person, not a book.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述自由人，而非书。

items.example: The verb turned the state into an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把状态变成动作。

items.example: Liberation names the change, not the condition.
The unit liberated the town at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 部队在黎明解放了小镇。

items.example: Liberty of speech has limits in law.
items.exampleCN: 言论自由在法律上有边界。

items.example: The word later became a political label.
items.exampleCN: 这个词后来成为政治标签。

items.example: The movement had a liberatory aim.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动带有解放目标。

latinEntries.structure: liber, libera, liberum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: n. 仲裁人，公断人；（引申）最终裁定者
definition_en: An independent person appointed to hear a dispute and give a decision that the parties have agreed to accept; by extension, anyone whose judgement settles a question.
core_image: 坐在两造中间、最后拍板的那个人
scene: 双方各让一步，接受了仲裁人的裁定。 Both sides accepted the arbitrator's ruling.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arbitrator 指被指定来听审并裁断争议的中立第三方。

pos.zh: 仲裁人；公断人；最终裁定者

senses.title: The appointed decider
senses.definition: a neutral person chosen by the parties, or by a body, to hear evidence and impose a settlement
senses.definitionCN: 由双方或某机构选定的中立者，听取证据并作出有约束力的解决方案
senses.example: The union and the firm could not agree on an arbitrator.
senses.exampleCN: 工会与公司无法就仲裁人人选达成一致。
senses.why: The ending -or marks the doer, so arbitrator is simply the one who arbitrates, the person inside the process.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -or 标记施动者，所以 arbitrator 就是「做仲裁的那个人」，是程序里的那个人。

senses.title: The final authority on a question
senses.definition: by extension, a person or thing whose judgement is treated as settling a matter of taste or value
senses.definitionCN: 引申指其判断被视为能定论品味或价值问题的人或事物
senses.example: Time is the only arbitrator of literary reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 时间是文学声誉唯一的裁定者。
senses.why: The legal role is borrowed as a metaphor: whoever ends the argument occupies the middle chair, even with no contract.
senses.whyCN: 法律角色被借作比喻：谁能终止争论，谁就坐上了中间那把椅子，哪怕并无合同。

intro.en: Arbitrator is the Latin agent noun from arbitrari, to judge, itself from arbiter, a witness who goes to see. English took both arbiter and arbitrator.
intro.cn: arbitrator 是拉丁语 arbitrari「裁断」的施动名词，而 arbitrari 出自 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」。英语把 arbiter 与 arbitrator 都吸收了。

items.en: Arbiter meant a witness who goes to look and then judges, from ad-, to, plus baetere, to come.
items.cn: arbiter 指前去看情况再作判断的见证人，由 ad-「向」加 baetere「来」构成。

items.en: The verb arbitrari meant to weigh a matter and decide it, the neutral ancestor of both English words.
items.cn: 动词 arbitrari 意为「权衡并裁定」，是两个英语词的中性祖先。

items.en: Adding -or, the doer ending, gave arbitrator, the person who performs the judging.
items.cn: 加上表施动者的 -or 得到 arbitrator，即执行裁断的那个人。

items.en: Anglo-French legal writing spelled it arbitratour, the form English courts used in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语法律文献拼作 arbitratour，这是 14 世纪末英国法院使用的形式。

items.en: English kept both forms: arbiter for any decisive authority, arbitrator for the appointed legal role.
items.cn: 英语保留了两种形式：arbiter 泛指有定论权的权威，arbitrator 专指被指定的法律角色。

items.en: Today an arbitrator is named in the clause, and the award carries the force of a court judgement.
items.cn: 如今仲裁人在条款中被指定，其裁决具有法院判决的效力。

note.en: The look-alike group separates arbiter, the wider word, from arbitrator, the appointed role, and warns against arbitrary; the near-meaning group lists other neutral deciders.
note.cn: 形近组把泛指的 arbiter 与专任的 arbitrator 分开，并提醒别与 arbitrary 混淆；近义组列出其他中立裁断者。

entries.definition: Anyone with power to decide.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有定论权的人。

entries.definition: To judge between two sides.
entries.definitionCN: 在双方之间裁断。

entries.definition: Decided by whim, not reason.
entries.definitionCN: 凭兴致而非依理决定。

entries.definition: One who helps sides agree.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助双方谈成的人。

entries.definition: A person who gives a formal ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 作出正式裁定的人。

entries.definition: An official who enforces the rules.
entries.definitionCN: 执行规则的裁判。

entries.definition: An official who settles play.
entries.definitionCN: 裁定比赛的人。

entries.definition: One who judges value or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 评定价值或质量的人。

normalIntro.en: Arbitrator is arbitrate plus -or: the person who does the arbitrating, sitting in the middle chair.
normalIntro.cn: arbitrator 就是 arbitrate 加 -or：做仲裁的那个人，坐在中间那把椅子上。

normal.en: Arbitrator is the appointed role; arbiter is the wider word.
normal.cn: arbitrator 是专任角色，arbiter 是泛指说法。

normal.en: A mediator only helps; an arbitrator decides.
normal.cn: mediator 只帮谈，arbitrator 直接定。

normal.en: The decision is an award, and it binds the parties.
normal.cn: 裁定叫 award，对双方有约束力。

normal.en: Sole arbitrator means one person, not a panel.
normal.cn: sole arbitrator 指独任一人，不是小组。

normal.en: Do not mix arbitrator with arbitrary, which means capricious.
normal.cn: 别把 arbitrator 与 arbitrary「反复无常」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a third chair between two arguing sides.
abstract.cn: 想象争执双方之间的第三把椅子。

abstract.en: Imagine a signature that ends a two-year quarrel.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名结束两年争吵。

abstract.en: Think of time as the judge nobody appointed.
abstract.cn: 想象时间这位没人指定的裁判。

examples.en: The arbitrator heard both sides for three days.
examples.cn: 仲裁人听双方陈述听了三天。

examples.en: Two arbitrators were replaced for a conflict of interest.
examples.cn: 两名仲裁人因利益冲突被更换。

examples.en: She acted as sole arbitrator in the shipping dispute.
examples.cn: 她在这起航运争议中担任独任仲裁人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arbitrate「仲裁」+ -or「人」——做仲裁的那个人，就是 arbitrator。

root: 拉丁语 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」生出 arbitrari「裁断」，加施动后缀 -or 成 arbitrator「裁断者」；英语 14 世纪末吸收，与泛指的 arbiter 分工并存。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the middle chair: the person appointed to end a dispute, and anyone whose word ends an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是中间那把椅子：被指定来终结争议的人，以及一句话就能终结争论的任何人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person seated between the two sides who makes the final call
core.cn: 核心意象：坐在两造中间、最后拍板的那个人

branches.en: A neutral named in the clause.
branches.cn: 条款中指定的中立者。

branches.en: Three days of hearing both sides.
branches.cn: 听双方陈述的三天。

branches.en: Time judging literary reputation.
branches.cn: 裁定文学声誉的时间。

branches.en: A critic whose word ends debate.
branches.cn: 一句话终止争论的评论家。

branches.en: Both occupy the middle chair.
branches.cn: 两者都坐在中间那把椅子上。

intro.en: Arbitrator is arbitrate plus the doer suffix -or, the same ending that builds actor, mediator and adjudicator.
intro.cn: arbitrator 是 arbitrate 加施动后缀 -or，同一词尾还构成 actor、mediator 与 adjudicator。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arbiter, arbitrari and the agent noun arbitrator; -or is the Latin doer ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arbiter、arbitrari 与施动名词 arbitrator；-or 是拉丁语的施动者词尾。

latinEntries.example: Arbiter is the base of the family.

definition_zh: 蒸馏；提炼；使滴下；（液体）渗出
definition_en: to purify or separate a liquid by boiling it into vapour and condensing it, or to extract the essential part of something
core_image: 蒸气在弯管里走一段，管壁上慢慢挂满水珠，最后汇成一滴落下
scene: 实验室里，学生加热烧瓶，蒸气在弯管壁上凝成水珠，最后汇成一滴滴进接收瓶。 The apparatus distilled the mixture into two separate liquids.
sceneCN: 这里 distill 指用加热汽化再冷凝的方式分离液体（第 1 个义项：蒸馏分离）；句意为这套装置把混合物蒸馏成两种分开的液体。图中可辨识物件：烧瓶、弯管、水珠、接收瓶。

pos.zh: 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提纯或分离；提炼（思想、经验）；使滴下
（液体）滴下、渗出

senses.title: To separate a liquid by boiling and condensing
senses.titleCN: 用加热汽化再冷凝的方式分离液体
senses.definition: to purify or separate a liquid by turning it into vapour and then cooling it back into liquid
senses.definitionCN: 把液体变成蒸气再冷却回液体，以提纯或分离
senses.example: The plant distills seawater into drinking water.
senses.exampleCN: 这套设备把海水蒸馏成饮用水。
senses.why: distill comes from Latin distillare 'to drip down', so the verb describes vapour being made to fall as drops.
senses.whyCN: distill 出自拉丁 distillare「滴下」，这个动词描述的是让蒸气成滴落下。

senses.title: To draw a strong spirit from a mash
senses.definition: to make a strong alcoholic drink by distilling a fermented liquid
senses.definitionCN: 通过蒸馏发酵液制成烈性酒
senses.example: They distill the fruit into a strong spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这种水果蒸馏成烈酒。
senses.why: alcohol boils before water, so distillation is the classic way to draw it off, and the verb took on the trade.
senses.whyCN: 酒精比水先沸腾，蒸馏正是把它抽出的经典办法，这个动词便承接了这一行业。

senses.title: To extract the essential part
senses.titleCN: 提炼思想或经验的精华
senses.definition: to reduce a large body of material to its essential content, as if separating a clear liquid from a muddy one
senses.definitionCN: 把大量材料缩减为本质内容，如同从浑浊液中分出清液
senses.example: The book distills twenty years of research into one volume.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书把二十年研究提炼成一册。
senses.why: the laboratory operation becomes a mental one: what matters is what survives the heat of selection.
senses.whyCN: 实验室操作变成头脑里的操作：要紧的，是在挑选的加热中留下来的部分。

senses.title: To drip, of a liquid
senses.definition: to come out in drops, said of liquid falling from a surface or through a small opening
senses.definitionCN: 以滴状流出，指液体从表面或小口落下
senses.example: Water distilled from the roof into the gutter.
senses.exampleCN: 水从屋顶滴进排水沟。
senses.why: the oldest sense is simply 'to drip down', and it survives beside the technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「滴下」，它与技术义并存至今。

senses.title: To form drops from vapour
senses.definition: to cause vapour to condense into droplets on a cool surface
senses.definitionCN: 使蒸气在冷表面上凝结成小水珠
senses.example: Cold glass distills the vapour into droplets.
senses.exampleCN: 冷玻璃使蒸气凝成小水珠。
senses.why: condensation is the second half of distilling, and the verb can name that half alone.
senses.whyCN: 冷凝是蒸馏的后半段，这个动词可以单独命名这一半。

senses.title: To reduce a text to its points
senses.titleCN: 从大量材料中提取要点
senses.definition: to shorten a long report or argument to its main points without losing the essential meaning
senses.definitionCN: 把长报告或论证缩到要点，而不丢失本质含义
senses.example: The editor distilled the report to a single page.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把报告提炼成了一页。
senses.why: a text is treated like a mixture: the water goes, the flavour stays.
senses.whyCN: 文本被当作混合物：水走了，味道留下。

senses.title: To purify by removing the rest
senses.definition: to purify a substance by leaving behind whatever does not vaporize at the chosen temperature
senses.definitionCN: 把在所选温度下不汽化的东西留下，从而提纯物质
senses.example: The process distills the oil until it is clear.
senses.exampleCN: 这个过程把油蒸馏到清澈为止。
senses.why: purity in distillation is not added but subtracted: everything else is left in the flask.
senses.whyCN: 蒸馏中的纯度不是加上去的，而是减出来的：其余一切都留在烧瓶里。

senses.title: To keep the core and drop the rest
senses.definition: used figuratively of any act of keeping what is essential and letting the incidental go
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指任何保留本质、放走偶然成分的行为
senses.example: Good teaching distills a subject without thinning it.
senses.exampleCN: 好的教学把一门学问提炼，却不把它冲淡。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps both parts of the image: heat selects, and condensation preserves.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留意象的两半：火负责挑选，冷凝负责保存。

intro.en: Distill comes from Latin distillare 'to drip down', from de- 'down' plus stillare 'to drip', from stilla 'a drop'. English has used the verb since the fourteenth century, with the British spelling distil. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: distill 来自拉丁 distillare「滴下」，由 de-「向下」加 stillare「滴」构成，后者出自 stilla「一滴」。英语自十四世纪使用这个动词，英式拼写为 distil。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stilla meant 'a drop', and its deeper origin is not established; any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: stilla 意为「一滴」，其更深来源没有定论，为其提出的更古老词根属于重构。

items.en: Stillare 'to drip' described liquid falling drop by drop, a plain physical verb before it became a technical one.
items.cn: stillare「滴」描述液体一滴一滴落下，在成为技术词之前是一个朴素的实体动词。

items.en: De- 'down' plus stillare gave distillare 'to drip down', which alchemists used for vapour collected as drops.
items.cn: de-「向下」加 stillare 构成 distillare「滴下」，炼金术士用它指把蒸气以滴状收集。

items.en: English distill appears in the fourteenth century for both the dripping and the apparatus, and the spelling distil is usual in British usage.
items.cn: 英语 distill 在十四世纪同时指滴落与器具，英式用法通常拼作 distil。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the verb was used for extracting the essence of writing and experience, not only of liquids.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个动词已用于提取写作与经验的精华，不只用于液体。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of stilla is unsettled, so any root offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：stilla 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，为其提出的任何词根都是重构形式，而非已证实的形式。

note.en: Group one holds the noun and apparatus of the same family, which share the dripping root; group two holds verbs for taking an essential part out of something.
note.cn: 第一组是同一家族的名词与器具，共享「滴」词根；第二组是表示从某物中取出本质部分的动词。

entries.definition: The process or its product; the verb names the act that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或产物；动词命名产生它的动作。

entries.definition: The vessel used for distilling; it comes from the same dripping root, not from the adverb meaning 'even now'.
entries.definitionCN: 用于蒸馏的容器；出自同一「滴」词根，不来自表示「仍然」的副词。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus stillare: to drip an idea into someone, hence to implant it gradually.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 stillare：把观念滴进某人心里，因此指逐渐灌输。

entries.definition: The condensed liquid collected from the apparatus, named after the action rather than the action itself.
entries.definitionCN: 从装置收集到的冷凝液，以动作命名而非动作本身。

entries.definition: To take a substance out with a solvent or force; no vaporizing is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 用溶剂或外力取出物质；不涉及汽化。

entries.definition: To remove impurities and improve quality; distilling is one way to refine a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 去除杂质、提高品质；蒸馏是精炼液体的一种方式。

entries.definition: To make something pure by any means, of which distilling is one.
entries.definitionCN: 用任何手段使某物纯净，蒸馏是其中一种。

entries.definition: To turn vapour into liquid or to make a text shorter; it covers only one stage of distilling.
entries.definitionCN: 使蒸气变液，或使文本变短；只覆盖蒸馏的一个阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: De- 'down' plus stillare 'drip': the verb is 'to make drip down'.
normal.cn: de-「向下」加 stillare「滴」：这个动词就是「使滴下」。

normal.en: The family runs distill, distil, distillation, distillate, distillery.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 distill、distil、distillation、distillate、distillery。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical sense: distill water, distill alcohol.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：蒸馏水、蒸馏酒精。

normal.en: The figurative phrases mark the rest: distill the essence, distill into one volume.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配标出其余义项：提炼精华、提炼成一册。

normal.en: British spelling doubles nothing: distil, distilled, distilling.
normal.cn: 英式拼写不双写词尾字母：distil、distilled、distilling。

abstract.en: Picture dew forming on a cold pipe and running into a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象冷管上结出露水，流进罐子里。

abstract.en: Picture a long letter cut to the one paragraph that matters.
abstract.cn: 想象一封长信被删到唯一要紧的那一段。

abstract.en: Picture a muddy pond producing a glass of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象一潭泥水变出一杯清水。

examples.en: The refinery distills crude oil into separate fuels.
examples.cn: 炼油厂把原油蒸馏成不同的燃料。

examples.en: She distilled the interview transcripts into four themes.
examples.cn: 她把访谈记录提炼成四个主题。

examples.en: Rainwater distilled through the canvas and dripped onto the floor.
examples.cn: 雨水透过帆布渗下，滴到地板上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dis（分开）+ till（滴）」——让汽一滴滴落下、分开成分：蒸馏、提炼

root: 拉丁 distillare「滴下」= de-（向下）+ stillare（滴）；stillare 出自 stilla（一滴），stilla 更深来源不确定。英式拼写 distil。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one dripping: a liquid is boiled and condensed, a spirit is drawn off, an essence is extracted, drops fall, vapour condenses, a text is shortened, impurities are left behind, and finally only the core is kept.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次滴落：液体被煮沸再冷凝，烈酒被抽出，精华被提取，液滴落下，蒸气凝结，文本被缩短，杂质被留下，最后只保留核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vapour travelling along a cool tube, gathering into beads, then falling as one drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒸气沿着冷管走，聚成水珠，最后落成一滴。

branches.en: SEPARATION AND PURITY: distilling separates by boiling point and purifies by subtracting what stays behind.
branches.cn: 分离与纯净：蒸馏按沸点分离，并通过减去留下的部分达到纯净。

branches.en: THE STILL TRADE: drawing spirits off a mash is the oldest commercial use of the same process.
branches.cn: 蒸馏行业：从发酵醪中抽出烈酒，是同一过程最古老的商业用途。

branches.en: REDUCING MATERIAL: extracting an essence and shortening a report both drop the incidental.
branches.cn: 缩减材料：提取精华与缩短报告，都在放走偶然成分。

branches.en: DRIPPING AND CONDENSING: the plain physical sense and the laboratory half-step are one movement of water.
branches.cn: 滴落与凝结：朴素的实体义与实验室的半步，是同一次水的运动。

branches.en: KEEPING THE CORE: heat selects and condensation preserves, which is what good distillation means in thought.
branches.cn: 保留核心：火负责挑选，冷凝负责保存，这正是思想上「好的提炼」的意思。

intro.en: Distill is a Latin verb of dripping, and its prefix and root also build the apparatus, the product and the word for implanting an idea.
intro.cn: distill 是一个表示「滴」的拉丁动词，其前缀与词根还构成器具、产物与「灌输观念」的词。

latinIntro.en: Stilla 'a drop' gives stillare and distillare; de- 'down' marks direction, and in- 'in' gives instill.
latinIntro.cn: stilla「一滴」衍生 stillare 与 distillare；de-「向下」标记方向，in-「进入」构成 instill。

items.example: The root names the single drop.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名单独的一滴。

items.example: The prefix points the fall downward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把滴落指向下方。

items.example: The Latin verb begins the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词开启词族。
他们把混合物蒸馏两次。

items.example: The unit distills a thousand litres a day.
items.exampleCN: 这台设备每天蒸馏一千升。

items.example: The plant is distilling the new batch.

items.meaning: a place where distilling is done
items.example: The distillery stands beside the river.

definition_zh: 退化；降解；品质下降；地位或尊严的降低
definition_en: the process of falling to a lower quality, condition, rank or structural state
core_image: 一块塑料样片在紫外灯下慢慢泛黄、开裂，最后一捏就碎
scene: 实验室的架子上，一块塑料样片在紫外灯下泛黄开裂，手指一捏就碎。 Ultraviolet light caused degradation of the sample within weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 degradation 指「材料因光照、氧化等作用而逐渐失去原有性能」（第 4 个义项：材料退化与老化）；句意为紫外光在几周内使样片发生降解。图中可辨识物件：塑料样片、紫外灯、泛黄裂纹、碎屑。

pos.zh: 退化；降解；降级；品质或尊严的降低

senses.title: A general fall in quality or condition
senses.titleCN: 品质或状况的总体下降
senses.definition: the process by which something loses quality, value or good condition over time
senses.definitionCN: 某物随时间失去品质、价值或良好状态的过程
senses.example: Ultraviolet light caused degradation of the sample within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外光在几周内使样片发生降解。
senses.why: The word is de- 'down' plus gradus 'step', so degradation is a movement down one grade rather than a sudden collapse.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 de-「向下」加 gradus「台阶」，因此 degradation 是往下走一个等级，而非突然崩塌。

senses.title: Land and soil degradation
senses.definition: the loss of soil fertility, structure or cover through erosion, salinity, compaction or overuse
senses.definitionCN: 因侵蚀、盐渍化、压实或过度使用而失去肥力、结构或覆盖
senses.example: Continuous cropping sped up the degradation of the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 连作加快了山坡的退化。
senses.why: Soil is a slowly renewed body, so its degradation is measured in decades and is hard to reverse.
senses.whyCN: 土壤是缓慢更新的整体，其退化以十年计，且难以逆转。

senses.title: Chemical breakdown of a substance
senses.definition: the breaking of large molecules into smaller ones by heat, light, water or microbial action
senses.definitionCN: 大分子因热、光、水或微生物作用而断裂为较小分子
senses.example: The polymer's degradation released a faint acid smell.
senses.exampleCN: 这种聚合物的降解释放出一股淡淡的酸味。
senses.why: Chemistry uses the word for the loss of a molecule's structure, which is a literal stepping down of complexity.
senses.whyCN: 化学用这个词指分子结构的丧失，也就是复杂度的字面「降级」。

senses.title: Material degradation in service
senses.definition: the loss of strength, colour or function in a material through corrosion, wear, heat or radiation
senses.definitionCN: 材料因腐蚀、磨损、热或辐射而失去强度、颜色或功能
senses.example: Salt air caused steady degradation of the bridge cables.
senses.exampleCN: 含盐的海风使桥梁缆索持续退化。
senses.why: Engineering watches degradation as a rate, because safety depends on how fast a material steps down.
senses.whyCN: 工程把退化看作一个速率，因为安全取决于材料下降得多快。

senses.title: Social or moral debasement
senses.definition: the lowering of a person or group to a condition of humiliation, exploitation or loss of dignity
senses.definitionCN: 使人或群体陷入屈辱、剥削或失去尊严的状态
senses.example: The report described the degradation of workers in the camps.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了营地里工人所受的贬损。
senses.why: The word's oldest English sense is a falling from dignity, and it still carries moral weight.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的英语义项是「从尊严上跌落」，至今仍带道德分量。

senses.title: Ceremonial loss of rank
senses.definition: the formal stripping of a title, office or rank, once performed in public ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式剥夺头衔、职务或军阶，旧时在公开仪式中执行
senses.example: The old rite of degradation removed the knight's belt and spurs.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的降级礼卸下了骑士的腰带与马刺。
senses.why: This is the literal sense of de- plus gradus: a person is moved down a step of the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 这是 de- 加 gradus 的字面义：一个人被移下等级阶梯的一级。

senses.title: Habitat degradation in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中的栖息地退化
senses.definition: the loss of a habitat's structure and species composition while some of it remains
senses.definitionCN: 栖息地仍有部分留存，但其结构与物种组成已丧失
senses.example: Draining the marsh caused habitat degradation for nesting birds.
senses.exampleCN: 排干沼泽造成了营巢鸟类的栖息地退化。
senses.why: Ecology needs a word for partial loss, because a habitat can be ruined without being erased.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要一个词指「部分丧失」，因为栖息地可以已经被毁，却并未消失。

senses.title: Signal or data degradation
senses.definition: the loss of clarity, accuracy or resolution in a transmitted signal or stored dataset
senses.definitionCN: 传输信号或存储数据集在清晰度、准确度或分辨率上的损失
senses.example: Repeated copying caused degradation of the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 反复复制使这段录音出现劣化。
senses.why: Information theory borrowed the word because quality can step down through a chain without anything being added.
senses.whyCN: 信息论借用这个词，因为品质可以在一连串环节中下降，而并未添加任何东西。

senses.title: Abstract: erosion of institutional trust
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：制度与信任的侵蚀
senses.definition: a transferred use for the gradual weakening of standards, trust or co-operation in an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 转指组织内标准、信任或合作的逐渐削弱
senses.example: Repeated exceptions led to degradation of the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 一再例外导致安全规则逐渐失效。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the staircase: each small exception is one step down, and the height is lost a step at a time.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了楼梯：每一次小小的例外都是一级台阶，高度是一级一级失去的。

intro.en: Degradation came to English from French and Latin, built on gradus 'step'. Its first English sense was a falling away from a former state, and the rank sense followed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: degradation 经法语与拉丁语进入英语，构自 gradus「台阶」。它最早的英语义项是「从原有状态跌落」，降级义随后出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gradus meant 'step, degree', from the verb gradi 'to walk'. The deeper origin of gradi is not established; the root commonly proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: gradus 意为「台阶、等级」，出自动词 gradi「行走」。gradi 的更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的词根是重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: De- 'down' plus gradus produced degradare 'to lower in rank', used first of clergy and officials moved down the hierarchy.
items.cn: de-「向下」加 gradus 构成 degradare「降低等级」，最初用于被移下等级的教士与官员。

items.en: Old French degradacion and English degradation appear in the fourteenth century with the sense of deterioration or degeneration, a falling from a former condition.
items.cn: 古法语 degradacion 与英语 degradation 在十四世纪出现，指恶化、变质，即从原有状态跌落。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word also named the public ceremony that stripped a knight or officer of rank.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词也指公开剥夺骑士或军官职级的仪式。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries chemistry, materials science and ecology adopted the word for the breakdown of substances, structures and habitats.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，化学、材料科学与生态学采用这个词来指物质、结构与栖息地的崩解。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of gradi, first date of the scientific sense): the walking root behind gradus is unsettled, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the chemical or ecological sense, so its date is approximate; any older form offered for gradi is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（gradi 的更深来源、科学义的首见年代）：gradus 背后「行走」的词根无定论，化学义与生态义的最早书证也无定论，年代只能约计；凡为 gradi 给出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same gradus stock that differ in grammar or sense; group two holds other words for falling quality, each stressing a different kind of loss.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 gradus 词干、语法或含义不同的词；第二组是其他表示品质下降的词，各自强调不同的损失。

entries.definition: To lower something in quality or rank; degradation is the process or result the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物品质或等级下降；degradation 是动词所产生过程或结果。

entries.definition: A series of steps or stages, from the same gradus root; it names an orderly scale, not a fall.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列台阶或阶段，同出 gradus 词根；它指有序的刻度，而非跌落。

entries.definition: Happening by small steps, from gradus; the adjective describes pace, not loss of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步发生的，出自 gradus；这个形容词描述节奏，而非品质损失。

entries.definition: To raise something to a higher grade; it reverses the de- of degradation while using the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物提升到更高等级；它与 degradation 的 de- 方向相反，却用同一词根。

entries.definition: Any worsening of condition; it is broader and less technical than degradation.
entries.definitionCN: 状况的任何恶化；它比 degradation 更宽泛、更少技术性。

entries.definition: Slow rotting or decomposition, especially of organic matter; degradation also covers metals, data and rank.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的腐烂或分解，尤指有机物；degradation 还涵盖金属、数据与等级。

entries.definition: The lowering of value, purity or dignity, as of coinage or character; it is a moral or monetary word.
entries.definitionCN: 价值、纯度或尊严的降低，如货币成色或人格；它是道德或货币领域的词。

entries.definition: Chemical attack on a metal surface; it is one cause of material degradation.
entries.definitionCN: 对金属表面的化学侵蚀；它是材料退化的一个原因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: De- 'down' plus gradus 'step': degradation is one step down the staircase.
normal.cn: de-「向下」加 gradus「台阶」：degradation 就是楼梯下了一级。

normal.en: The same root gives grade, gradual, graduate, upgrade and downgrade.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 grade、gradual、graduate、upgrade 与 downgrade。

normal.en: The family runs degrade, degraded, degradable, degradative and degradability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 degrade、degraded、degradable、degradative 与 degradability。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: land degradation, chemical degradation, material degradation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：土地退化、化学降解、材料退化。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was moral: a falling from dignity, not a falling of soil.
normal.cn: 最早的英语义项是道德性的：从尊严跌落，而非土壤流失。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where each step is worn a little lower than the one before.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，每一级都比上一级磨得更低。

abstract.en: Picture a copied tape played again and again until the voice blurs.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘磁带被反复翻录，声音渐渐糊掉。

abstract.en: Picture a rule broken once for convenience, then again, until nobody cites it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则为图方便被破一次，再破一次，直到没人再提它。

examples.en: Heat and moisture accelerate the degradation of the coating.
examples.cn: 热与湿气加快涂层的退化。

examples.en: Land degradation lowered the yield of the whole district.
examples.cn: 土地退化降低了大片地区的产量。

examples.en: The term also names the degradation of a person's dignity.
examples.cn: 这个词也指一个人尊严的贬损。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「de（向下）+ grad（台阶）+ ation」——品质往下走一级 → 退化、降解

root: 拉丁 degradare「降低等级」= de-（向下）+ gradus「台阶」，gradus 出自 gradi「行走」，gradi 的更深来源不确定；英语义最早指「从原有状态跌落」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one staircase: a higher condition exists, a step is taken downward, quality falls, structure breaks, standing falls, and finally the same image describes signals and institutions.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一段楼梯展开：本来处在较高状态，向下走一级，品质下降，结构断裂，地位跌落，最后同一意象描述信号与制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step worn lower than the one before it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一级比上一级磨得更低的台阶。

branches.en: GENERAL AND LAND: any quality can step down, and soil is the slowest case to repair.
branches.cn: 总体与土地：任何品质都能下台阶，土壤是最慢修复的一种。

branches.en: MATTER: molecules break apart and materials lose strength by the same downward movement.
branches.cn: 物质：分子断裂与材料失强，是同一种向下的运动。

branches.en: HUMAN STANDING: dignity and rank fall on the same scale as quality.
branches.cn: 人的地位：尊严与职级同品质一样沿同一尺度下落。

branches.en: HABITAT: a place can be degraded while still partly standing.
branches.cn: 栖息地：一个地方可以已经退化，却仍部分存在。

branches.en: TRANSFER: signals and trust lose resolution the way materials lose strength.
branches.cn: 转移：信号与信任失去清晰度，正如材料失去强度。

intro.en: Degradation is a Latin-derived noun with a prefix, a step root and an action suffix, and the root also builds a large English family.
intro.cn: degradation 是拉丁来源名词，含前缀、台阶词根与动作后缀，这个词根还构成一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradus gives grade, gradation, gradual, graduate, degrade, upgrade and downgrade; de- adds 'down'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gradus 衍生 grade、gradation、gradual、graduate、degrade、upgrade 与 downgrade；de- 添「向下」。

items.example: The prefix marks the downward direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出向下的方向。

items.example: The rank was one gradus below the other.
items.exampleCN: 这个等级比另一个低一级。

items.example: The root image is walking down a stair.
items.exampleCN: 词根意象是沿楼梯往下走。

items.example: The suffix makes the process a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把过程变成名词。

items.meaning: to lower in quality or rank

items.example: The degradation was visible in the cracks.
items.exampleCN: 退化从裂纹上就能看出。
这种覆盖物完全可降解。

items.example: The gradation from light to dark was smooth.
items.exampleCN: 从浅到深的过渡很平滑。

items.meaning: to raise to a higher grade

definition_zh: 加速；加速度；增速
definition_en: the process of going faster, or the rate at which speed increases
core_image: 仪表盘上猛抬的速度指针：速度在变大
scene: 绿灯亮起，赛车手踩下油门，指针瞬间冲向表盘右端。 The car's acceleration amazed everyone at the track.
sceneCN: 这里 acceleration 是「加速（过程）」（第 1 个义项：速度加快的过程）；句意为这辆车的加速令赛道边所有人惊叹。

pos.zh: 加速；加快
加速度（物理量）

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「加速」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「加快的」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「加速器；油门」

senses.title: The act of speeding up
senses.definition: the process of starting to move or happen faster
senses.definitionCN: 开始更快移动或更快发生的过程
senses.example: The rocket climbed with smooth acceleration.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭平稳加速攀升。
senses.why: The noun names the action behind the verb accelerate: speed as something that grows, not just is.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名动词 accelerate 背后的动作：速度是被孕育增长的，而非静止不变。

senses.title: The rate of increase in physics
senses.definition: in physics, the change of speed per unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中，单位时间内速度的变化量
senses.example: Earth's gravity gives falling objects an acceleration of about nine point eight metres per second squared.
senses.exampleCN: 地球引力使落体获得约每秒九点八米平方的加速度。
senses.why: Science fixed the loose idea of 'going faster' into an exact quantity: speed divided by time.
senses.whyCN: 科学把「越走越快」的模糊观念精确为确定的量：速度除以时间。

senses.title: An increase in pace of events
senses.definition: a rise in the pace or rate of an activity or development
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动或发展节奏、速率的提升
senses.example: The acceleration of urban change shocked older residents.
senses.exampleCN: 城市变迁的提速让老居民震惊。
senses.why: Anything that can run faster can also develop faster, so the physical image widened to time and history.
senses.whyCN: 任何能跑得更快的东西也可以「发展得更快」，于是物理图像扩展到时间与历史。

intro.en: Acceleration comes from Latin acceleratio, built on accelerare 'to hasten', from ad- 'toward' and celer 'swift'.
intro.cn: acceleration 来自拉丁语 acceleratio，基于 accelerare（使加快），由 ad-（向）与 celer（迅速）构成。

items.en: The root *kel- suggested swift movement, feeding Latin celer.
items.cn: 词根一般认为与「迅速运动」相关，成为拉丁语 celer 的来源。

items.en: celer meant swift, as in celeritas 'speed'.
items.cn: celer 意为迅速，如 celeritas（速度）。

items.en: ad- plus celerare meant to hasten something.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 加 celerare 意为使某物加快。

items.en: The noun acceleratio named the hastening itself.
items.cn: 名词 acceleratio 指加快这一行为本身。

items.en: English took the word, and physics later gave it exact meaning.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，物理学后来赋予其精确含义。

note.en: The first group gathers the celer- word family; the second gathers words for speeding up.
note.cn: 第一组收 celer- 词族；第二组收表示提速的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同根动词，即本词的基础。

entries.definition: A device or pedal that speeds things up.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指加速器或油门。

entries.definition: Swiftness of movement, from the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同根书面语名词，义为「迅速」。

entries.definition: An increase in speed, often informal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提速」，多口语。

entries.definition: Quickness of action, with a hint of rushing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「匆忙」，带仓促意味。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to become faster.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快」。

entries.definition: The rate of slowing down.
entries.definitionCN: 反义名词，义为「减速」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the swift root celer and the physics formula; the abstract hooks picture the needle climbing.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「迅速」词根 celer 与物理公式；抽象记忆点想象指针攀升。

normal.en: Break it as ac-celer-ation: celer means swift in Latin.
normal.cn: 拆为 ac-celer-ation：celer 在拉丁语中意为迅速。

normal.en: The -ion ending turns the verb accelerate into a noun.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ion 把动词 accelerate 变为名词。

normal.en: In physics, acceleration equals change of speed over time.
normal.cn: 物理学中，加速度等于速度变化除以时间。

normal.en: Gravity's acceleration on Earth is about nine point eight.
normal.cn: 地球重力加速度约为九点八。

normal.en: Pressing the accelerator pedal gives the car acceleration.
normal.cn: 踩下油门（accelerator）使车获得加速度。

abstract.en: Picture a speedometer needle sweeping to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象速度表指针向右猛扫。

abstract.en: Picture a falling apple gaining speed each second.
abstract.cn: 想象落下的苹果每秒都在提速。

abstract.en: Picture a city changing faster every year.
abstract.cn: 想象城市逐年加速变迁。

examples.en: The train's acceleration pinned passengers gently to their seats.
examples.cn: 列车的加速让乘客轻微地压向椅背。

examples.en: Engineers measured the acceleration of the prototype on the test track.
examples.cn: 工程师在试验道上测量了样车的加速度。

examples.en: Economists debated whether the acceleration of growth could last.
examples.cn: 经济学家争论增长的提速能否持续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞勒雷申」——谐音「可加速了的申（请）」，一踩油门就提速。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ celer（迅速）→ accelerare（使加快）→ acceleratio（加速）；核心义是「速度向快处推进」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the everyday act of speeding up, to the exact physics quantity, to the pace of change in life.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从日常的提速行为，到精确的物理学量，再到生活变迁的节奏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: speed that is not fixed but growing
core.cn: 核心意象：速度不固定，而是在增长

branches.en: A vehicle or process starting to run faster.
branches.cn: 车辆或过程开始跑得更快。

branches.en: Speed change fixed as a measurable quantity.
branches.cn: 速度变化被固化为可测的量。

branches.en: Both senses describe speed as something that increases.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把速度描述为在增加的东西。

branches.en: The faster rhythm of cities, markets, and history.
branches.cn: 城市、市场与历史更快的节奏。

branches.en: Exact measure in physics, loose measure in social change.
branches.cn: 物理中的精确度量，社会变迁中的宽泛度量。

intro.en: The word joins the toward-prefix with the swift stem and the action noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由「向」前缀、「迅速」词干与动作名词后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin celer and acceleratio are direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the stem and the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 celer 与 acceleratio 是直接祖先，拉丁条目记录词干与名词。

definition_zh: v. 漂白，使变白；n. 漂白剂
definition_en: to make something white or pale with chemicals or strong sunlight; a chemical used for this
core_image: 一件带黄渍的白衬衫泡在漂白水里，污渍一圈圈褪成白
scene: 她把白衬衫泡进漂白水里，第二天污渍全没了。 She soaked the white shirt in bleach and by morning the stain was gone.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bleach 作名词指漂白剂、作动词指漂白；句意是她把白衬衫泡进漂白水，次日污渍全消。

pos.zh: 漂白；使褪色变白
漂白剂

senses.title: To whiten cloth with chemicals
senses.definition: to remove colour or stains from cloth, paper or hair using a chemical agent
senses.definitionCN: 用化学药剂除去织物、纸张或头发上的颜色与污渍
senses.example: Cheap paper yellows quickly unless it is bleached.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价纸张若不漂白，很快就会发黄。
senses.why: Old English blǣcan meant to whiten, and the noun bleach is simply that action turned into a substance.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 blǣcan 意为使变白，名词 bleach 就是把这个动作变成一种物质。

senses.title: To be paled by sunlight
senses.definition: to lose colour through strong sunlight, so that a surface turns pale
senses.definitionCN: 因强烈日照而失色，表面变得苍白
senses.example: The curtains had been bleached to a thin grey.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘被晒成了一种淡淡的灰。
senses.why: Sun does slowly what chemicals do fast, so the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 阳光慢慢做的，正是化学品快速做的，于是同一动词兼指两者。

senses.title: The chemical itself
senses.definition: a liquid or powder that whitens and disinfects
senses.definitionCN: 能使物件变白并消毒的液体或粉剂
senses.example: Do not mix bleach with ammonia in the same bucket.
senses.exampleCN: 不要把漂白剂与氨水倒进同一个桶里。
senses.why: A verb naming an action often becomes a noun naming the stuff that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 表示动作的动词常转为表示施行该动作之物的名词。

intro.en: Bleach goes back to Old English blǣcan, to whiten, from blāc, pale, the same root that gives bleak.
intro.cn: bleach 上溯古英语 blǣcan（使变白），源自 blāc（苍白的），与 bleak 同根。

items.en: Blāc means pale or shining white.
items.cn: blāc 意为苍白、亮白。

items.en: Blǣcan is the verb to make pale or white.
items.cn: blǣcan 是「使变苍白、变白」的动词。

items.en: The verb appears in early English for whitening cloth.
items.cn: 该动词在早期英语中指漂白布料。

items.en: Lye and sour milk serve as the first bleaching agents.
items.cn: 碱液与酸牛奶是最早的漂白剂。

items.en: Open-air bleaching fields give their name to bleachers.
items.cn: 露天漂白场把自己的名字给了「露天看台」。

items.en: Bleach now means chlorine or oxygen bleach in a bottle.
items.cn: 现代 bleach 多指瓶装的含氯或含氧漂白剂。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the bl- start; the near-meaning group separates the colour change from the chemical that causes it.
note.cn: 形近组保留 bl- 开头；近义组把「变白的过程」与「造成它的药剂」分开。

entries.definition: Cold and without shelter or hope.
entries.definitionCN: 阴冷荒凉、没有希望。

entries.definition: To lose blood.
entries.definitionCN: 流血。

entries.definition: To draw back in fear.
entries.definitionCN: 因恐惧而退缩。

entries.definition: To make pale, or to boil briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 使变苍白；焯水。

entries.definition: To make or become white.
entries.definitionCN: 使变白；变白。

entries.definition: To make something less dark.
entries.definitionCN: 使变浅、变亮。

entries.definition: To become paler over time.
entries.definitionCN: 渐渐褪色。

entries.definition: To clean something of germs.
entries.definitionCN: 杀灭物体上的病菌。

normalIntro.en: Bleach is the act of making pale, and the same word became the bottle that does it.
normalIntro.cn: bleach 本是「使变苍白」这个动作，同一个词又变成做这件事的瓶子。

normal.en: Blāc meant pale, and bleach is what makes pale.
normal.cn: blāc 意为苍白，bleach 就是使之苍白。

normal.en: Bleak and bleach share that old pale root.
normal.cn: bleak 与 bleach 共享那个古老的「苍白」词根。

normal.en: Sunlight bleaches curtains; chemicals bleach shirts.
normal.cn: 阳光漂白窗帘；化学品漂白衬衫。

normal.en: Add -er and you get bleacher, once a whitening field.
normal.cn: 加 -er 得 bleacher，原指漂白场。

normal.en: The noun and the verb live in one word.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同住一个词里。

abstract.en: Colour removed rather than added.
abstract.cn: 不是加上颜色，而是拿走颜色。

abstract.en: A stain turning into nothing.
abstract.cn: 污渍化作无形。

abstract.en: Whiteness bought with a chemical.
abstract.cn: 用化学品买来的白。

examples.en: Never bleach silk at home.
examples.cn: 不要在家漂白丝绸。

examples.en: The deck had been bleached by ten summers.
examples.cn: 甲板被十个夏天的日头晒得发白。

examples.en: Keep bleach away from the ammonia.
examples.cn: 把漂白剂放得离氨水远些。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不劣质」——漂白剂一下去，再劣质的布也白得发亮。

root: 古英语 blǣcan（使变白）← blāc（苍白的）；与 bleak 同源

sensesIntro.en: Two agents and one result: chemical, sunlight, or the bottle itself, all ending in white.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种力量、一个结果：化学品、阳光，或那瓶药水，最后都落在「白」上。

core.cn: 核心意象：一件带渍的白衬衫进桶，出来时已无颜色

branches.cn: 在桶里泡了一夜的白衬衫。

branches.en: A paper mill smelling of chlorine.
branches.cn: 带氯气味的造纸厂。

branches.en: Curtains turned thin grey by sun.
branches.cn: 被晒成淡灰的窗帘。

branches.en: A bottle with a warning label.
branches.cn: 贴着警告标签的瓶子。

branches.en: Whiteness made by a liquid.
branches.cn: 由液体造成的白。

definition_zh: 在野党；反对党；与执政方相对的政党
definition_en: the political party, or the largest party, that is not in government and opposes the governing side
core_image: 议会大厅里，执政者坐在一边，另一边的人站起来逐条挑错，桌上摆着另一份预算
scene: 议事厅里两排长椅相对，一份预算刚发下，另一排人立刻翻到附录逐行质疑。 The opposition party demanded a full debate on the budget.
sceneCN: 议事厅里两排长椅相对，一份预算刚发下，另一排人立刻翻到附录逐行质疑；句中的这个说法指「不在政府内、以反对执政方为职责的政党」（第 1 个义项：选举后未掌权、在议会中与政府相对的那一个政党）。图中可辨识物件：两排长椅、预算册、附录页、麦克风、记者的笔记本。

pos.zh: 在野党；反对党（可数）
（作定语）在野党的；反对党的

senses.title: The party out of office
senses.definition: the party that lost or did not enter government and now sits outside the executive
senses.definitionCN: 未能执政或未进入政府、如今置身行政机构之外的政党
senses.example: The opposition party has promised to reverse the cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 在野党承诺要撤销这些削减。
senses.why: Parliament is arranged as two facing benches: whoever does not sit on the government bench sits opposite it.
senses.whyCN: 议会排成两排相对的座椅：不坐政府那一排的人，就坐在它的对面。

senses.title: The official or largest opposition
senses.titleCN: 官方反对党或最大反对党
senses.definition: the opposition party formally recognized as the main alternative, with special rights and funding
senses.definitionCN: 被正式认定为主要替代选项的反对党，享有特定权利与经费
senses.example: The official opposition party receives a state allowance for research.
senses.exampleCN: 官方反对党获得国家拨付的研究经费。
senses.why: A chamber needs one recognizable voice to answer the government, so the largest opposing group is given that role.
senses.whyCN: 议事机构需要一个可辨认的声音来回应政府，于是最大的反对团体被赋予这一角色。

senses.title: The mirror in a two-party system
senses.definition: in a system with two dominant parties, the one currently outside office
senses.definitionCN: 在两强主导的制度中，当下不掌权的那一个政党
senses.example: In a two-party system the opposition party is simply the other half of the seesaw.
senses.exampleCN: 在两党制下，在野党不过是跷跷板的另一半。
senses.why: With only two large options, the opposition is not a small critic but the government-in-waiting.
senses.whyCN: 只有两个大选项时，在野党不是小小的批评者，而是候任政府。

senses.title: The shadow cabinet role
senses.definition: the group of opposition politicians who mirror each minister and prepare alternative policies
senses.definitionCN: 由在野政治人物组成、一一对应各部并准备替代政策的一组人
senses.example: Each opposition party spokesperson is paired with a minister.
senses.exampleCN: 反对党每位发言人都与一位部长对应。
senses.why: To be ready to govern, the party out of office builds a duplicate cabinet that watches each department.
senses.whyCN: 为了随时能够执政，在野党会搭一个复制版内阁，逐个盯住各部。

senses.title: A party built to challenge
senses.titleCN: 为挑战执政党而组建的党
senses.definition: a party founded mainly to displace the governing side rather than to defend an old interest
senses.definitionCN: 主要为了取代执政方、而非维护旧有利益而成立的政党
senses.example: The new opposition party was founded by mayors from three regions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新的反对党由三个地区的市长创立。
senses.why: Some parties begin as movements against a government; their first programme is often simply 'not them'.
senses.whyCN: 有些政党起初就是反对现政府的运动，其第一份纲领往往只是「不要他们」。

senses.title: Opposition on a local council
senses.definition: the group on a town or city council that opposes the local administration
senses.definitionCN: 在镇议会或市议会中与地方行政当局相对的团体
senses.example: The local opposition party forced a review of the bus routes.
senses.exampleCN: 地方在野党促成了对公交线路的复核。
senses.why: The same facing benches appear in miniature wherever a council meets.
senses.whyCN: 只要议事机构开会，同样的一对座椅就会以缩小的形式出现。

senses.title: An opposition alliance
senses.definition: several opposition parties acting together to challenge one government
senses.definitionCN: 若干个在野政党共同行动、挑战同一个政府
senses.example: Four opposition parties formed an alliance before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 四个反对党在投票前结成了联盟。
senses.why: When one party is too small to face the government alone, several opposing parties line up on the same bench.
senses.whyCN: 当一个政党太小、无法独自面对政府时，几个反对党就排到同一条长椅上。

senses.title: The scrutiny function
senses.definition: the job of questioning ministers, demanding documents and publicizing failures
senses.definitionCN: 质询部长、索取文件并把失误公之于众的职责
senses.example: The opposition party used its committee seats to request the reports.
senses.exampleCN: 反对党利用它在委员会的席位索要那些报告。
senses.why: A party without power still holds a function: it keeps the government's answers on the record.
senses.whyCN: 没有权力的政党仍有一项职能：把政府的回答留在记录里。

intro.en: The phrase joins opposition, from Latin opponere 'to place against', with party, from Latin pars 'part'. English speakers combined them as parliamentary benches took their modern shape; the first use is not securely dated.
intro.cn: 这个说法把出自拉丁语「放到对面」的名词，与出自拉丁语「部分」的名词拼在一起。英语使用者把两者组合起来，大约与议会两排座椅形成现代格局同时；首次使用的时间不能确证。

items.en: Ob- 'against' plus ponere 'place' produced opponere 'to set against'. Its participle oppositus gave opposition.
items.cn: 意为「对着」的前缀加「放」构成表示「放到对面」的动词，其分词形式后来给出「反对」这一名词。

items.en: Pars, partis meant 'part, share'. Through Old French it gave English party, first a part or a side.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词意为「部分、份」，经古法语给出英语中表示「一部分」或「一方」的名词。

items.en: Old French opposition and partie carried both halves toward English, where they were later joined in one phrase.
items.cn: 古法语中表示「反对」与「部分」的两个词分别把两半带进英语，后来才被拼进同一个短语。

items.en: From the eighteenth century, writers began to speak of the party in opposition, meaning the side facing the ministers. The exact first use of the full phrase is uncertain.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，作者们开始说「处于反对地位的政党」，指面对部长们的那一方。完整短语的首见时间不确定。

items.en: As disciplined parties and mass electorates grew, the label became a fixed parliamentary term, with an official leader and a shadow team.
items.cn: 随着纪律严明的政党与大规模选民出现，这个说法成为固定的议会术语，并配有正式领袖与影子团队。

items.en: The phrase now travels beyond Westminster and describes any party outside government, from a city council to a national assembly.
items.cn: 如今这个说法已走出英国议会，可指任何不掌权的政党，从市议会到国民议会皆可。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two halves or a very close form; the second group names the other seats and alliances around a government.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个组成部分之一，或形式极近；第二组指政府周围的其他席位与联盟。

entries.definition: The act of resisting or the whole side that opposes. It can name a camp without naming a single organized party.
entries.definitionCN: 指抵抗的行为或整个反对阵营。它可以指一个阵营，却不必指某一个有组织的政党。

entries.definition: The one-word noun is far broader: a gathering, a legal side or any political group. The phrase adds the specific role.
entries.definitionCN: 单用的名词宽得多：聚会、法律上的一方或任何政治团体；加上前面的修饰后才指出具体角色。

entries.definition: A loyal supporter of a side, often one who will not listen to the other. It never names the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方的忠实支持者，往往不听另一方的话。它从不指制度本身。

entries.definition: The adjective for the side that argues against. It can describe a team or a lawyer, not only a parliamentary group.
entries.definitionCN: 指持反对立场的那一方的形容词，可形容球队或律师，不限于议会团体。

entries.definition: The party that holds office and answers for the government. It is the exact opposite seat to the phrase in question.
entries.definitionCN: 指掌握职位、为政府作答的政党，正好是本条所指席位的对面。

entries.definition: A party with fewer seats than the largest one. It may be an opposition party or merely a small partner in a coalition.
entries.definitionCN: 指席位少于最大党的政党。它可能是在野党，也可能只是联盟中的小伙伴。

entries.definition: A deal among several parties to act together. An opposition party is one organization; a coalition may contain several.
entries.definitionCN: 指若干政党共同行动的协议。在野党是一个组织，联盟则可能包含好几个。

entries.definition: A person or group competing for the same prize. It stresses competition, while the phrase stresses institutional position.
entries.definitionCN: 指为同一目标竞争的人或团体。它强调竞争，而本条短语强调制度位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real components, the parliamentary picture of facing benches, real derived words and fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的构件、议会里两排相对座椅的画面、真实派生词与固定搭配。

normal.en: The first half means 'placed against'; the second half means 'part'. Together: the part placed against the government.
normal.cn: 前半段意为「放到对面」，后半段意为「部分」；合起来就是「被放到政府对面的那部分人」。

normal.en: The official opposition is the largest opposing group, and it receives money and staff for the role.
normal.cn: 官方反对党就是最大的反对团体，并因此获得经费与人员。

normal.en: Its mirror is the party that holds office, sitting on the other bench.
normal.cn: 它的镜像就是掌握职位、坐在另一条长椅上的政党。

normal.en: The family runs opposition, oppositional, oppose, opponent and partisan.
normal.cn: 同族词包括反对、对立的、反对、对手与党派支持者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the role: the official opposition party, the largest opposition party, an opposition spokesperson.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：官方反对党、最大在野党、反对党发言人。

abstract.en: Picture two benches facing each other across a narrow aisle; the empty one is not empty for long.
abstract.cn: 想象两条长椅隔着窄窄的过道相对；空着的那条不会空太久。

abstract.en: The party out of office is a government folded up and stored, waiting for the next election to unfold it.
abstract.cn: 在野党就是被折叠收起的政府，等下一次选举把它展开。

abstract.en: Its daily work is not to win but to keep the other bench answering out loud.
abstract.cn: 它每天的工作不是取胜，而是让对面那条长椅大声作答。

examples.en: The opposition party tabled an alternative budget within an hour of the speech.
examples.cn: 反对党在演讲结束后一小时内提交了一份替代预算。

examples.en: An opposition party with only twelve seats can still force a recorded vote.
examples.cn: 只有十二个席位的在野党仍能迫使进行记名投票。

examples.en: The opposition party's shadow team met the teachers' union before the review.
examples.cn: 反对党的影子团队在复核前会见了教师工会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧波季申·帕提」——先「欧」到对面「波」一下，再「季申」自己的方案，最后带上自己的那一「派」，正是对着政府的在野党

root: 前半出自拉丁 opponere「放到对面」（ob-「对着」+ ponere「放」）的分词 oppositus 与名词 oppositio；后半经古法语上溯到拉丁 pars/partem「部分、份」。合起来即「被放到政府对面的那部分人」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same bench: a party out of office, sometimes officially recognized, sometimes one half of a two-party mirror, and always carrying a shadow team and a duty to scrutinize.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一条长椅展开：不掌权的政党，有时被正式认定，有时是两党镜像的另一半，并且始终带着影子团队与监督职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bench that faces the government and keeps it answering.
core.cn: 核心意象：面向政府、逼它作答的那条长椅。

branches.en: OUT AND CHALLENGING: one simply sits outside office; the other was founded to push the governing side aside.
branches.cn: 在外与来挑战：一个只是坐在政府之外，另一个从成立起就是要挤走执政方。

branches.en: RECOGNIZED MIRROR: the largest opposing group gets formal rights, and in a two-party system the mirror is the whole alternative.
branches.cn: 被承认的镜像：最大的反对团体获得正式权利；在两党制下，这面镜子就是全部的替代选项。

branches.en: SHADOW AND SCRUTINY: a duplicate cabinet prepares policy while the same members demand documents and answers.
branches.cn: 影子与监督：一套复制内阁准备政策，同一批成员则索要文件与答复。

branches.en: LOCAL SCALE: the same facing benches appear in a town hall, with the same function in miniature.
branches.cn: 地方尺度：同样的相对座椅出现在市政厅，职能只是缩小了。

branches.en: JOINED BENCH: several opposing parties may line up together when none is strong enough alone.
branches.cn: 合并的长椅：当没有一个足够强大时，几个反对党可以排到一起。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two Latin roots, one meaning 'place against' and one meaning 'part', each with its own English family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁词根构成，一个意为「放到对面」，一个意为「部分」，各自都带一串英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin opponere supplies the first element through its participle and noun; Latin pars, partem supplies the second through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中意为「放到对面」的动词经其分词与名词提供第一段；拉丁语中意为「部分」的名词经古法语提供第二段。

items.meaningCN: 处于对面的状态，语义偏移为「反对、反对阵营」
items.exampleCN: 这项动议虽有反对仍然通过。

items.meaningCN: 具有反对性质的，语义偏移为「对立的」
items.example: The group took an oppositional stance.
items.exampleCN: 该团体采取了对立姿态。

items.meaningCN: 把自己放到对面，语义偏移为「反对」
items.exampleCN: 两位部长反对这项法案。

items.meaningCN: 被放到对面的，语义偏移为「相反的、对面的」
items.example: The office is opposite the library.

items.meaningCN: 被放到对面的人，语义偏移为「对手」

items.structure: part- (Latin pars, partem 'part') + -y (noun suffix through Old French -ie)
items.meaningCN: 部分或一方，语义偏移为「政党」
items.example: The party held its conference in June.

items.structure: part- + -isan (adherent suffix via French and Italian)
items.meaningCN: 某一方的跟随者，语义偏移为「党徒、偏袒的」
由两方共同支持的，语义偏移为「跨党派的」
items.exampleCN: 这项法案赢得跨党派支持。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 放到对面；被放到对面的

definition_zh: 植被；某一地区全部植物；（医学）赘生物
definition_en: the plant life of an area taken as a whole, especially what covers the ground; in medicine, an abnormal growth on a body surface
core_image: 一片土地被草木密密铺满，从贴地的苔藓一直连到高处的树冠，像一床会呼吸的绿被
scene: 沙丘表面只有薄薄一层草木；风一吹沙就移动，研究员靠记录这层草木的厚薄与种类判断沙丘是否稳定。 Thin vegetation holds the dunes together against the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetation 指「一个地区地表全部植物形成的覆盖层」（第 1 个义项：把一地植物整体看待）；句意为稀疏的植被把沙丘粘在一起，抵御风的搬运。

pos.zh: 植被；某一地区的全部植物（不可数）
（医学）赘生物；心瓣膜或体表长出的异常组织

derivatives.zh: 生长；像植物一样过呆板生活
营养生长的；植物状态的

senses.title: Collective plant life of a region
senses.titleCN: 一个地区整体看待的植物
senses.definition: the whole body of plants growing in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区生长的全部植物
senses.example: The vegetation of the island is mostly low scrub.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的植被以低矮灌丛为主。
senses.why: Vegetation is the noun of state built on vegetare 'to quicken, make lively': wherever plants take hold, the ground is made lively.
senses.whyCN: vegetation 是由表示「使有生气」的 vegetare 加名词后缀构成的状态名词：凡是植物扎下根的地方，土地就活了起来。

senses.title: The ground-covering layer
senses.titleCN: 贴地铺开、护住土壤的那一层
senses.definition: the layer of plants that covers the ground and protects the soil
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖地表并保护土壤的植物层
senses.example: Thin vegetation holds the dunes together against the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 稀疏的植被把沙丘粘在一起，抵御风。
senses.why: The collective sense narrows here to what touches the surface: roots bind grains, stems slow the wind, and the ground stops moving.
senses.whyCN: 整体义在此收窄为「接触地表」的部分：根抓住沙粒，茎挡住风，地面便不再移动。

senses.title: Rank or luxuriant growth
senses.titleCN: 长得过盛、几乎挡住路的草木
senses.definition: plants growing thickly and abundantly in a place
senses.definitionCN: 某地长得繁茂浓密的植物
senses.example: Vegetation grew thick along the irrigation ditch.
senses.exampleCN: 灌渠边的草木长得又密又高。
senses.why: When growth runs ahead of use, the word shifts from what is there to how much of it there is, and the tone becomes almost a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 当生长超出需要，词义就从「有什么」转向「有多少」，语气也近乎抱怨。

senses.title: A plant community or type
senses.titleCN: 按形态划分的一类植物群落
senses.definition: a class of plant community distinguished by its structure and species
senses.definitionCN: 按结构与物种划分出的植物群落类型
senses.example: Botanists classify the valley's vegetation into four formations.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把谷地的植被分为四个群系。
senses.why: Modern ecology turns the mass noun into a countable technical term: each formation is a named package of species and structure.
senses.whyCN: 现代生态学把这个不可数名词变成可数的术语：每个群系都是物种与结构组成的有名组合。

senses.title: The record made by a survey
senses.titleCN: 调查后绘制出的植被记录
senses.definition: the plants of an area as recorded, mapped or described by a survey
senses.definitionCN: 经调查、绘图或描述记录下来的植被
senses.example: The team finished a vegetation survey before the dam was built.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝动工前，团队完成了植被调查。
senses.why: Surveying fixes the living layer into data, so the same word now names a map, a list and a baseline for later comparison.
senses.whyCN: 调查把这层活的东西固定成资料，同一个词于是既指图，也指清单，还指日后比对的基线。

senses.title: What is cleared away
senses.titleCN: 被当作障碍清理掉的草木
senses.definition: plants regarded as an obstacle and removed from a site
senses.definitionCN: 被视为障碍而从场地清除的植物
senses.example: Workers cleared the vegetation around the new pipeline.
senses.exampleCN: 工人清除了新管线周围的植被。
senses.why: Once plants are in the way of a project, the word stops describing an ecosystem and starts describing material to be removed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦草木挡了工程的路，这个词就不再描述生态系统，而开始指待清除的对象。

senses.title: Abnormal tissue growth
senses.definition: a mass of abnormal tissue, especially on a heart valve or body surface
senses.definitionCN: 异常长出的组织块，尤指心瓣膜或体表上的
senses.example: Echocardiography showed a small vegetation on the valve.
senses.exampleCN: 超声心动图显示瓣膜上有一个小的赘生物。
senses.why: Medical Latin applied the plant-growth word to anything that sprouts where it should not, so the image of unwanted sprouting carries over.
senses.whyCN: 医学拉丁语把这个「植物生长」的词用到一切不该长却长出来的东西上，杂草蔓生的意象因此延续。

senses.title: Plant cover read as a climate record
senses.titleCN: 被当作气候档案来读的植被
senses.definition: past plant cover reconstructed from pollen, seeds or other traces
senses.definitionCN: 从花粉、种子等遗迹重建出的过去植物覆盖
senses.example: Pollen in the lake mud records how the vegetation changed.
senses.exampleCN: 湖泥里的花粉记录了植被如何变化。
senses.why: Because plant cover answers to rainfall and temperature, its fossil traces become a thermometer for ancient climates.
senses.whyCN: 植物覆盖随降水与温度而变，因此它的化石遗迹成了测量古气候的温度计。

intro.en: Vegetation comes from Medieval Latin vegetatio 'a quickening, growth', from vegetare 'to enliven', built on vegetus 'lively'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vegetation 来自中世纪拉丁 vegetatio「使有生气、生长」，源于 vegetare「使有生气」，再往前是 vegetus「有活力的」。年代为约数。

items.en: Vegere meant 'to be lively, active'. Its deeper origin is not settled, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: vegere 意为「有生气、活动着」。其更深来源没有定论，凡为它给出的印欧形式都是重构形式。

items.en: The participle vegetus 'lively, vigorous' supplied the adjective from which the verb was felt to come.
items.cn: 分词 vegetus「有活力的、精神抖擞的」提供了形容词，人们也觉得动词正是由它而来。

items.en: Vegetare 'to enliven, animate' produced Medieval Latin vegetatio 'a making lively, growth'.
items.cn: vegetare「使有生气、使活动」产生了中世纪拉丁 vegetatio「使有生气、生长」。

items.en: English adopted vegetation in the seventeenth century for the plant life of a region, and botany fixed it as a technical collective noun.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 vegetation，指一地的植物，植物学随后把它固定为技术性的集合名词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century physicians used vegetation for abnormal growths on valves and surfaces, borrowing the image of something sprouting.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，医生用 vegetation 指瓣膜与体表上的异常生长物，借的是「冒出来生长」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the link of vegere to vigere 'to be vigorous' is generally believed but not demonstrated, and the first English date for the botanical sense is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：vegere 与 vigere「强健」的联系一般认为成立，却未经证实；植物义在英语中的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that share the Latin root from one false friend; group two holds the words used for plant cover in ecology.
note.cn: 第一组区分共用拉丁词根的外形相近词与一个假朋友；第二组是生态学里指植物覆盖的近义词。

entries.definition: From vegetare, but in English it means to live a dull, inactive life or, of plants, simply to grow.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 vegetare，但在英语里指过呆板无所事事的生活，或指植物生长。

entries.definition: From Latin vegetabilis 'animating', the same root, but the noun settled on a garden crop.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vegetabilis「有生气的」，词根相同，名词却落在园圃作物上。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of plants' or 'plant-like', closer to the Latin source than vegetation is.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「植物的、像植物的」，比 vegetation 更贴近拉丁原义。

entries.definition: From venerari 'to worship', with no plant meaning at all; only the sound overlaps.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 venerari「敬拜」，与植物无关，只有读音重叠。

entries.definition: The plant species of a region listed by name; vegetation is the living cover itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个地区按名称列出的植物物种；vegetation 指活生生的覆盖本身。

entries.definition: Green plants seen as pleasant colour; it is a look, while vegetation is an ecological mass.
entries.definitionCN: 把绿色植物当作悦目的颜色；它说的是一种外观，vegetation 说的是生态整体。

entries.definition: A neutral everyday phrase with no technical edge; vegetation is its scientific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的日常说法，不带技术色彩；vegetation 是它的科学对应词。

entries.definition: The total mass of living material, measured by weight; vegetation names the cover, not the weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指活物质的总质量，按重量计；vegetation 指覆盖，不指重量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin family and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的拉丁词族与真实搭配，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: vegetare 'to enliven' + -ation: the state of ground made lively by plants.
normal.cn: vegetare「使有生气」+ -ation：土地被植物弄得有生气的状态。

normal.en: The family: vegetate, vegetative, vegetational, vegetated.
normal.cn: 同族：vegetate、vegetative、vegetational、vegetated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: natural vegetation, dense vegetation, sparse vegetation, native vegetation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：天然植被、茂密植被、稀疏植被、乡土植被。

normal.en: The same root gives vegetable and vegetal, both about plant life.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 vegetable 与 vegetal，都与植物有关。

normal.en: Medical charts speak of a vegetation on a valve, a sprout where nothing should sprout.
normal.cn: 病历上说瓣膜上有赘生物，即在不该长的地方长出一块。

abstract.en: Picture a lawn so thick that you cannot see the soil beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片厚到看不见下面泥土的草坪。

abstract.en: Picture a green blanket laid over a wound in the land.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿毯盖在土地的伤口上。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf where every plant of a valley is filed as one volume.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上有一卷书，把一个谷地的植物全归档在里面。

examples.en: Fires every few years keep the vegetation short and diverse.
examples.cn: 每隔几年烧一次，植被就保持低矮而多样。

examples.en: Loose vegetation was cleared before the foundations were poured.
examples.cn: 浇筑地基之前，松散的植被已被清除。

examples.en: The valley's vegetation shifts from grass to oak as you climb.
examples.cn: 沿山坡向上，谷地植被从草类变为橡树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维基（veget）+ 生长（ation）」——地上长满绿色档案 → 植被

root: 拉丁 vegetare「使有生气、促使生长」＝ vegere「有活力」＋反复后缀；vegetatio 指「生长」。vegere 更深来源不确定，与 vigere「强健」的联系一般认为成立但未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is made lively, the ground is covered, the cover is classified, mapped, cleared, and finally read either as disease or as climate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先使某处有生气，再铺满地面，然后被分类、绘图、清除，最后或被读成疾病，或被读成气候。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a living quilt spread over the ground, growing from below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一床铺在地面上的活被子，从下面长上来。

branches.en: QUICKENING: the root sense is making a place lively, whether mildly or rankly.
branches.cn: 使有生气：词根义就是让某处活起来，无论温和还是过盛。

branches.en: COVER: roots bind the surface, so the mass becomes a protective layer.
branches.cn: 覆盖：根抓住地表，整体于是成为保护层。

branches.en: CLASSIFY: ecology names formations, then fixes them into surveys.
branches.cn: 分类：生态学先给群系命名，再把它们固定为调查资料。

branches.en: OBSTACLE: what blocks a project turns from ecosystem into material to be removed.
branches.cn: 障碍：挡住工程的部分，从生态系统变成待清材料。

branches.en: TWO READINGS: growth may be disease in a body or evidence of ancient climate in mud.
branches.cn: 两种读法：生长既可能是体内的病，也可能是泥里的古气候证据。

intro.en: Vegetation is built from a Latin verb stem plus a noun suffix, and that stem also builds several everyday English words.
intro.cn: vegetation 由拉丁动词词干加名词后缀构成，这个词干还构成若干日常英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vegere 'to be lively' gives vegetus, vegetare, vegetatio; the suffix -ation marks an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vegere「有生气」给出 vegetus、vegetare、vegetatio；后缀 -ation 表示动作或其结果。

items.example: The bare stem carries the idea of life.
items.exampleCN: 光秃的词干带着「活」的意思。

items.example: The adjective describes ground that is full of growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述长满植物的土地。

items.example: Warm rain vegetates the dry slope.
The noun names the process, not the plants.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指过程，不指植物。

items.meaning: action or result of an action
items.example: It turns a verb stem into a nameable state.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词词干变成可命名的状态。

items.meaning: the state of ground made lively
to grow, or to live dully
items.example: Moss vegetates on the shaded wall.
items.exampleCN: 苔藓在背阴的墙上生长。

items.meaning: tending to grow rather than reproduce

items.example: The vegetated bank held the soil.
items.exampleCN: 长满植物的河岸保住了土壤。

definition_zh: 刺破；扎穿；刺出的小孔；[喻] 戳破（幻想、说法）
definition_en: to make a small hole in something with a sharp point, or the hole so made
core_image: 一枚钉子扎进车胎，气从一个小孔里嘶嘶漏掉
scene: 自行车的后胎被一枚钉子扎穿，气在半分钟里泄光。 A nail had punctured the back tyre, and the air was gone in half a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 puncture 指扎破车胎（第 1 个义项：刺破轮胎）；句意为自行车的后胎被一枚钉子扎穿，气在半分钟里泄光。

pos.zh: 刺破；扎穿
小孔；刺痕

senses.title: A punctured tyre
senses.definition: to make a small hole in something with a sharp point
senses.definitionCN: 用尖物在某物上扎出小孔
senses.example: A nail had punctured the back tyre, and the air was gone in half a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚钉子扎穿了后胎，气在半分钟里就漏光了。
senses.why: The verb names one sharp point entering a surface and leaving a narrow opening.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是动词，指一个尖点进入表面、只留下一个窄孔的动作。

senses.title: A puncture in the tyre
senses.definition: the small hole itself, or a tyre made flat by such a hole
senses.definitionCN: 那个小孔本身，或因这种小孔而瘪掉的轮胎
senses.example: The puncture was no wider than a pin, yet the whole tyre failed.
senses.exampleCN: 那个小孔不比针尖宽，整条轮胎却报废了。
senses.why: Here the noun names the result rather than the act, and British use lets it stand for a flat tyre.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是名词，命名的是结果而不是动作；英式用法里它还可以直接指瘪掉的轮胎。

senses.title: A puncture wound
senses.definition: a wound made by a sharp point driving into the body
senses.definitionCN: 尖锐物刺入身体造成的伤口
senses.example: The doctor cleaned the puncture wound before it could infect.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在感染之前清洗了那处刺伤。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the literal picture but narrows it to skin and flesh, where depth matters more than width.
senses.whyCN: 医学沿用这个字面画面，只把它收窄到皮肉上；在那里深度比宽度更要紧。

senses.title: To puncture a myth
senses.definition: to destroy a widespread claim, or to drain someone's confidence
senses.definitionCN: 击破一个广为流传的说法，或泄掉某人的信心
senses.example: One careful study punctured the myth that the market always corrects itself.
senses.exampleCN: 一项严谨的研究戳破了市场总会自我修正的神话。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows a small hole to describe a large claim losing its pressure.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借一个小孔，来描述一个庞大的说法失去压力。

intro.en: Puncture comes straight from Latin punctura, 'a prick', built on the verb pungere, 'to prick or sting'.
intro.cn: puncture 直接来自拉丁语 punctura（一刺），词根是动词 pungere（刺、螫）。

items.en: Pungere meant to prick, sting or pierce with a point.
items.cn: pungere 意为用尖物刺、螫或穿透。

items.en: Its participle punctus described something pricked or pointed.
items.cn: 它的分词 punctus 描述被刺过或带尖的东西。

items.en: Punctura named the prick itself and the small hole it left.
items.cn: punctura 指刺的动作本身以及留下的小孔。

items.en: English took the word first for wounds and small openings.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词指伤口和小开口。

items.en: Later it became a verb for deflating claims and confidence.
items.cn: 后来它变成动词，用来给说法和信心放气。

note.en: The look-alike group is the punct- family; the near-meaning group separates pierce, prick, perforate and stab by size and intent.
note.cn: 形近组是 punct 词族；近义组按大小与意图把「穿透」「轻刺」「穿孔」「捅刺」分开。

entries.definition: exactly on time.
entries.definitionCN: 准时的。

entries.definition: marks that divide written text.
entries.definitionCN: 划分书面文字的标点。

entries.definition: attentive to tiny details.
entries.definitionCN: 拘泥于细枝末节的。

entries.definition: sharp and stinging to the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 对感官有尖锐刺激的。

entries.definition: to go right through something.
entries.definitionCN: 径直穿透某物。

entries.definition: to make a tiny hole with a point.
entries.definitionCN: 用尖物扎出极小的孔。

entries.definition: to make a hole or holes through a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 在表面打出一个或多个孔。

entries.definition: to thrust a knife or point into something.
entries.definitionCN: 用刀或尖物捅入。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a nail, a small hole and a slow hiss.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一枚钉子、一个小孔、一丝慢漏气声」的画面。

normal.en: Puncture contains punct, the Latin point: a point does the work.
normal.cn: puncture 里有 punct（拉丁语的「点」）：干活的是那个尖点。

normal.en: Picture a nail lying on the road, waiting for one tyre.
normal.cn: 想象一枚钉子躺在路上，等着某条轮胎。

normal.en: The stress is on PUNCT; the second syllable is light.
normal.cn: 重音在 PUNCT，第二个音节很轻。

normal.en: The word ends like capture: something is taken out of the tyre.
normal.cn: 词尾像 capture：有东西从轮胎里被拿走了。

normal.en: A puncture is small, quiet and complete: that is why it works as a metaphor.
normal.cn: puncture 小、静、彻底：所以它能当比喻。

abstract.en: A puncture defeats size: a pin can ruin a tyre it could never move.
abstract.cn: puncture 击败体量：一根针能毁掉它根本推不动的轮胎。

abstract.en: The figurative sense always keeps the hiss: something solid loses pressure.
abstract.cn: 比喻义始终保留那声嘶响：坚固的东西失去了压力。

abstract.en: To puncture a claim is to leave it intact in appearance and empty in fact.
abstract.cn: 戳破一个说法，就是让它外形完好、内容空空。

examples.en: A nail had punctured the back tyre, and the air was gone in half a minute.
examples.cn: 一枚钉子扎穿了后胎，气在半分钟里就漏光了。

examples.en: One careful study punctured the myth that the market always corrects itself.
examples.cn: 一项严谨的研究戳破了市场总会自我修正的神话。

examples.en: The doctor cleaned the puncture wound before it could infect.
examples.cn: 医生在感染之前清洗了那处刺伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: punct（点）+ ure：尖点一扎，留下一个小孔。

root: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）的分词 punctus + 名词后缀 -ura

sensesIntro.en: Four senses keep one small hole: the act of pricking, the hole and the flat tyre it leaves, a wound in the body, and a claim deflated until it no longer holds air.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项围绕同一个小孔：扎孔的动作、孔本身与它造成的瘪胎、身体上的刺伤，以及被放到再也存不住气的说法。

core.en: A NAIL AND A HISSING TYRE
core.cn: 一枚钉子和一条嘶嘶漏气的轮胎

branches.en: The act of pricking and the hole it leaves.
branches.cn: 扎孔的动作与它留下的孔。

branches.en: A tyre that fails because of one narrow opening.
branches.cn: 因一个窄孔而报废的轮胎。

branches.en: Skin and flesh entered by a point.
branches.cn: 被尖点刺入的皮肤与肌肉。

branches.en: The same gesture aimed at a claim or a confidence.
branches.cn: 同一个动作指向说法或信心。

branches.en: The metaphor of a surface losing its air.
branches.cn: 表面失去气的比喻。

intro.en: The punct family is wide: puncture, punctual, punctuation and punctilious all come from the idea of a point that marks or divides.
intro.cn: punct 词族很宽：puncture、punctual、punctuation、punctilious 都来自「一个点用来标记或划分」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin pungere gives the verb, punctus the participle and punctura the noun; English kept the point in every member of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pungere 提供动词，punctus 提供分词，punctura 提供名词；英语在这一族的每个成员里都保留了那个「点」。

exact to the point of time
sharp and stinging to the senses

definition_zh: adj. 合成的，复合的 n. 合成物
definition_en: made of several parts combined

definition_zh: 浮夸；自负的做派；铺张的排场
definition_en: the quality of being self-important in speech, manner or display
core_image: 一个人把嗓门和姿势都放大一号，好让整个房间都看见他
scene: 主席台上的人清了三次嗓子才开口，那份排场让整个礼堂都发闷。 The speaker cleared his throat three times before beginning, and the pomposity of the ceremony made the hall feel airless.
sceneCN: 这里 pomposity 指仪式上的铺张排场（第 4 个义项：仪式铺张）；句意为台上的人清了三次嗓子才开口，那种排场让整个礼堂都发闷。

pos.zh: 浮夸；自负的做派；铺张的排场

senses.title: Inflated speech
senses.definition: language made larger than the thought behind it
senses.definitionCN: 语言被放得比它背后的想法更大
senses.example: The minister's pomposity turned a short answer into ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 部长那套浮夸把一个简短回答拖成了十分钟。
senses.why: The vice here is proportion: words outrunning meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这里的毛病是比例：言辞跑到了意义前面。

senses.title: Self-important manner
senses.definition: a bearing that asks to be taken seriously before anything has been said
senses.definitionCN: 还没开口就先要求被认真对待的姿态
senses.example: He entered every room with a pomposity that no joke could dent.
senses.exampleCN: 他进每个房间都带着一种玩笑撼不动的自负。
senses.why: The body performs the claim even when the mouth is silent.
senses.whyCN: 即使嘴不出声，身体也在表演那个主张。

senses.title: Institutional display
senses.definition: the ceremony an organisation stages to make its power visible
senses.definitionCN: 机构为让权力可见而搭起的仪式
senses.example: The bank's pomposity showed in its marble and its waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行的排场体现在大理石和等待时间上。
senses.why: Institutions borrow the word from people and make it architecture.
senses.whyCN: 机构从人那里借来这个词，然后把它变成建筑。

senses.title: Ceremonial display
senses.definition: the swell of robes, titles and announcements at a formal event
senses.definitionCN: 正式场合里袍服、头衔与宣告的层层堆叠
senses.example: The pomposity of the ceremony made the hall feel airless.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式的铺张让整个礼堂都发闷。
senses.why: This sense is about staging, not about any one speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎舞台布置，不关乎某一位说话者。

senses.title: Ornate prose
senses.definition: writing that prefers the long word and the balanced clause
senses.definitionCN: 偏爱长词与对仗句子的写作
senses.example: The essay's pomposity hides a very simple argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的夸饰掩着一个非常简单的论点。
senses.why: Style can be a way of making a small idea look furnished.
senses.whyCN: 文风可以让一个小想法看起来陈设齐全。

senses.title: Self-importance
senses.definition: a settled belief that one's own rank deserves attention
senses.definitionCN: 一种稳定的信念：自己的地位理应得到关注
senses.example: Her pomposity was not an act; she had believed it for years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的自命不凡不是表演；她已经信了很多年。
senses.why: Here the word names a belief rather than a performance.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词命名一种信念，而不是一场表演。

senses.title: Pomposity as mask
senses.definition: display used to cover uncertainty or a lack of substance
senses.definitionCN: 用来遮住不确定或内容不足的排场
senses.example: The pomposity of the new director was a shield for his fear.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管的浮夸是他恐惧的一面盾。
senses.why: The word can be read backwards, as a confession.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以反过来读，当成一句自白。

senses.title: Comic pomposity
senses.definition: the lovable version, where the speaker is undone by his own dignity
senses.definitionCN: 可爱的那一面：说话者被自己的尊严绊倒
senses.example: The chairman's pomposity was the best part of the annual dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 主席那份端架子是年度晚宴上最好看的部分。
senses.why: Comedy often needs the word to be dear rather than cruel.
senses.whyCN: 喜剧常需要这个词显得可亲，而不是刻薄。

intro.en: Pomposity is the noun of a procession: pomp was the show that walked through a city, and the word kept the swagger.
intro.cn: pomposity 是一场游行的名词：pomp 曾是穿过城市的展示，这个词留下了那份招摇。

items.en: Pompe meant 'a sending, a procession', the escort that walked a god or a ruler through a city.
items.cn: pompe 意为「送出、游行」，指护送神祇或统治者穿过城市的队列。

items.en: Latin pompa kept the sense of a public show with music and robes.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pompa 保留了那种带音乐与袍服的公开展示。

items.en: Late Latin pomposus meant 'full of display', and it carried a hint of excess from the start.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 pomposus 意为「充满排场」，从一开始就带着过度的暗示。

items.en: English took pompous, and pomposity followed as its noun.
items.cn: 英语借入 pompous，pomposity 作为其名词随后出现。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the noun was chiefly a criticism, as it still is.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个名词主要是一种批评，至今仍是。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pomp family; the near-meaning group separates pretension, grandiosity, bombast and mere pride.
note.cn: 形近组是 pomp 词族；近义组把「做作」「夸大」「浮词」与「单纯的自豪」分开。

entries.definition: a claim to importance one lacks.

entries.definition: a swollen sense of one's own scale.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己规模的膨胀感。

entries.definition: language inflated beyond its content.
entries.definitionCN: 超出内容的膨胀语言。

entries.definition: an exaggerated sense of one's worth.
entries.definitionCN: 对自身价值的夸大的感觉。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a man who has turned his voice and his chin up one size.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一个人把嗓门和下巴都放大一号」的画面。

normal.en: Pomposity holds pomp, the old word for a procession: the show is still walking.
normal.cn: pomposity 里藏着 pomp（古语里的游行）：那场展示还在走。

normal.en: Think of a speaker clearing his throat three times before a short sentence.
normal.cn: 想象一位说话者，短短一句话前清了三次嗓子。

normal.en: Pom-POS-i-ty: the stress sits on pos, and the word puffs itself up.
normal.cn: pom-POS-i-ty：重音落在 pos，整个词把自己吹了起来。

normal.en: Say pom-PAH-si-ti; the middle vowel opens wide like a held note.
normal.cn: 读成 pom-PAH-si-ti，中间那个元音张开得像一个拖长的音符。

normal.en: Pair it with airless: pomposity makes a room feel short of oxygen.
normal.cn: 把它和 airless 配对：浮夸让房间显得缺氧。

abstract.en: Pomposity is a matter of proportion: it is not size, but size without content.
abstract.cn: 浮夸是比例问题：不是大，而是没有内容的大。

abstract.en: The word began as the name of a parade and ended as a name for a bore.
abstract.cn: 这个词起初是一场游行的名字，最后成了无聊之人的名字。

abstract.en: Every pomposity contains a small fear that the audience will notice the gap.
abstract.cn: 每一份浮夸里都藏着一点恐惧：怕观众发现那个空隙。

examples.cn: 说话的人清了三次嗓子，那份浮夸让礼堂发闷。

examples.en: The essay's pomposity hides a very simple argument.

examples.en: The chairman's pomposity was the best part of the annual dinner.
examples.cn: 主席那份端架子是年度晚宴上最好看的部分。
